1	// Package backoff is the redelivery policy for transiently-failed JetStream
2	// deliveries: a NakWithDelay envelope — flat by default, optionally growing
3	// multiplicatively per delivery — bounded by MaxDeliver, with an optional
4	// Term on the final delivery.
5	//
6	// The policy owns disposition and delay calculation only, and nothing wider:
7	// dead-letter capture, domain metrics/logging, and the decision of which
8	// failures are transient stay with the caller. It drives both the modern
9	// [jetstream.Msg] API (NakOrTerm, NumDelivered, IsFinalDelivery) and the legacy
10	// *nats.Msg API (the NakOrTermLegacy / NumDeliveredLegacy / IsFinalDeliveryLegacy
11	// counterparts, over the [LegacyMsg] interface). Both surfaces share one
12	// implementation, so they behave identically; the legacy set is a transitional
13	// bridge for consumers not yet on the modern API and can be removed once none
14	// remain.
15	//
16	// Delay calculation ([Policy.DelayFor]) is independent of message disposition:
17	// it is a pure function of the delivery count, so a caller can pin or meter the
18	// delay envelope without a message in hand.
19	//
20	// # Zero-value and unlimited semantics
21	//
22	// MaxDeliver matches [jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver]: a non-positive value
23	// (0 or [UnlimitedMaxDeliver]) means unlimited redeliveries, so no delivery is
24	// ever final and NakOrTerm always Naks. Note this reads zero differently from
25	// jsconsumer.Config.MaxDeliver, where 0 means "default to DefaultMaxDeliver":
26	// bridge with jsconsumer.Config.EffectiveMaxDeliver() (never the raw field), so
27	// an unset consumer MaxDeliver becomes the real default here instead of
28	// unlimited. Missing message metadata (a synthetic test message) reads as the
29	// first delivery — base NakDelay, never final — the safe default being another
30	// retry, not a Term.
31	//
32	// The Term-on-exhaustion posture is the COR-762 fix, lifted from
33	// mirror-pipeline's fanoutengine: on the final delivery a Nak is dropped
34	// silently by the broker (MaxDeliver reached), and on a WorkQueue stream the
35	// un-acked message then orphans — pinning the oldest-pending-age gauge — until
36	// StreamMaxAge finally expires it. Terming instead removes it cleanly. Streams
37	// where lingering is acceptable (a webhook stream whose max_age doubles as the
38	// retry backstop) leave TermOnExhaustion off and keep the plain Nak.
39	//
40	// Dead-letter capture stays with the caller, which should capture BEFORE
41	// disposing — gate it on [IsFinalDelivery]:
42	//
43	//	if backoff.IsFinalDelivery(msg, p.MaxDeliver) {
44	//		captureToDLQ(ctx, msg)
45	//	}
46	//	outcome, err := p.NakOrTerm(msg)
47	package backoff
48	
49	import (
50		"fmt"
51		"math"
52		"time"
53	
54		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
55		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
56	)
57	
58	// UnlimitedMaxDeliver is the explicit Policy.MaxDeliver value for unlimited
59	// redeliveries (matching jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver, where a
60	// non-positive value disables the delivery cap). The zero value means the same
61	// thing; the named constant lets a caller say so on purpose.
62	const UnlimitedMaxDeliver = -1
63	
64	// Outcome is the disposition NakOrTerm chose, for the caller's metrics and
65	// logs.
66	type Outcome string
67	
68	const (
69		OutcomeNak  Outcome = "nak"
70		OutcomeTerm Outcome = "term"
71	)
72	
73	// Policy is the redelivery envelope a consumer applies to transient
74	// failures. MaxDeliver must match the consumer's on-server MaxDeliver — the
75	// policy detects the final delivery by comparing against it.
76	type Policy struct {
77		// NakDelay is the base delay before redelivery, and with a zero Factor
78		// the whole envelope: flat suits failures expected to clear on their own
79		// timetable, with MaxDeliver bounding the total.
80		NakDelay time.Duration
81		// Factor is the optional multiplicative growth per prior delivery: the
82		// Nth delivery naks with NakDelay × Factor^(N-1), capped at MaxDelay.
83		// Values ≤ 1 (including the zero value) keep the flat envelope. Growing
84		// envelopes suit failures that get cheaper to wait out than to retry —
85		// a downstream in a crash loop, a rate limit — where hammering on the
86		// flat cadence spends MaxDeliver too fast.
87		Factor float64
88		// MaxDelay caps the grown delay; it does nothing for a flat policy.
89		// Zero with a growing Factor leaves growth bounded only by MaxDeliver
90		// ending the redeliveries (the computed delay still saturates rather
91		// than overflowing).
92		MaxDelay time.Duration
93		// MaxDeliver is the consumer's redelivery cap
94		// (jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver). Non-positive (0 or
95		// UnlimitedMaxDeliver) means unlimited redeliveries — matching the
96		// jetstream field's semantics — so no delivery is ever final and NakOrTerm
97		// always Naks.
98		MaxDeliver int
99		// TermOnExhaustion makes the final delivery Term instead of Nak, so a
100		// work-queue message is removed cleanly rather than orphaning un-acked
101		// (COR-762). Callers with a DLQ capture before calling NakOrTerm.
102		TermOnExhaustion bool
103	}
104	
105	// LegacyMsg is the subset of the legacy *nats.Msg that the *Legacy redelivery
106	// entry points drive — Nak-with-delay, Term, and the delivery metadata. *nats.Msg
107	// satisfies it; a test can stub it.
108	type LegacyMsg interface {
109		NakWithDelay(delay time.Duration, opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
110		Term(opts ...nats.AckOpt) error
111		Metadata() (*nats.MsgMetadata, error)
112	}
113	
114	// NakOrTerm applies the policy to a transiently-failed modern [jetstream.Msg]
115	// delivery: NakWithDelay (see [Policy.DelayFor]) for redelivery, or — on the
116	// final delivery with TermOnExhaustion set — Term. Without TermOnExhaustion the
117	// final delivery still Naks; the broker drops the Nak at MaxDeliver and the
118	// stream's retention decides the message's fate.
119	//
120	// The returned Outcome reports which disposition was chosen, for the caller's
121	// metrics and logs. A disposition error is worth a log line but nothing more:
122	// a failed Nak redelivers via AckWait expiry anyway, and a failed Term on a
123	// work-queue stream means the message lingers exactly as it would have without
124	// the policy.
125	func (p Policy) NakOrTerm(msg jetstream.Msg) (Outcome, error) {
126		return p.nakOrTerm(modernDisposer{msg})
127	}
128	
129	// NakOrTermLegacy is [Policy.NakOrTerm] for a legacy *nats.Msg delivery,
130	// behaving identically over the [LegacyMsg] API.
131	func (p Policy) NakOrTermLegacy(msg LegacyMsg) (Outcome, error) {
132		return p.nakOrTerm(legacyDisposer{msg})
133	}
134	
135	// nakOrTerm is the disposition shared by the modern and legacy entry points.
136	func (p Policy) nakOrTerm(d disposer) (Outcome, error) {
137		if p.TermOnExhaustion && isFinalDelivery(d, p.MaxDeliver) {
138			if err := d.term(); err != nil {
139				return OutcomeTerm, fmt.Errorf("term on final delivery: %w", err)
140			}
141			return OutcomeTerm, nil
142		}
143		if err := d.nakWithDelay(p.DelayFor(deliveryCount(d))); err != nil {
144			return OutcomeNak, fmt.Errorf("nak with delay: %w", err)
145		}
146		return OutcomeNak, nil
147	}
148	
149	// DelayFor reports the redelivery delay the policy applies after delivery
150	// number numDelivered (1 on first delivery): NakDelay for a flat policy,
151	// NakDelay × Factor^(numDelivered-1) capped at MaxDelay for a growing one.
152	// numDelivered ≤ 1 — including the 0 that [NumDelivered] reports when
153	// metadata is unavailable — reads as the first delivery. Exposed so a caller
154	// can log or meter the delay it is about to apply.
155	func (p Policy) DelayFor(numDelivered int) time.Duration {
156		if p.Factor <= 1 || numDelivered <= 1 {
157			return p.NakDelay
158		}
159		d := float64(p.NakDelay) * math.Pow(p.Factor, float64(numDelivered-1))
160		if p.MaxDelay > 0 && d >= float64(p.MaxDelay) {
161			return p.MaxDelay
162		}
163		if d >= float64(math.MaxInt64) {
164			// Uncapped growth outran time.Duration; saturate instead of wrapping
165			// negative (a negative NakWithDelay would redeliver immediately).
166			return math.MaxInt64
167		}
168		return time.Duration(d)
169	}
170	
171	// NumDelivered reports the JetStream delivery count of a modern [jetstream.Msg]
172	// (1 on first delivery), or 0 if metadata is unavailable (e.g. a synthetic test
173	// message).
174	func NumDelivered(msg jetstream.Msg) int {
175		return deliveryCount(modernDisposer{msg})
176	}
177	
178	// NumDeliveredLegacy is [NumDelivered] for a legacy *nats.Msg.
179	func NumDeliveredLegacy(msg LegacyMsg) int {
180		return deliveryCount(legacyDisposer{msg})
181	}
182	
183	// IsFinalDelivery reports whether this is the last delivery before JetStream
184	// stops redelivering (NumDelivered has reached MaxDeliver), so a transient
185	// failure here is terminal rather than another Nak-and-retry. A non-positive
186	// maxDeliver means unlimited redeliveries (the jetstream.ConsumerConfig
187	// semantics), so no delivery is final — without the guard the zero value
188	// would read every delivery as final and Term on the first failure.
189	// Unavailable metadata also reads as non-final: the safe default is another
190	// retry, not a Term.
191	func IsFinalDelivery(msg jetstream.Msg, maxDeliver int) bool {
192		return isFinalDelivery(modernDisposer{msg}, maxDeliver)
193	}
194	
195	// IsFinalDeliveryLegacy is [IsFinalDelivery] for a legacy *nats.Msg.
196	func IsFinalDeliveryLegacy(msg LegacyMsg, maxDeliver int) bool {
197		return isFinalDelivery(legacyDisposer{msg}, maxDeliver)
198	}
199	
200	// disposer is the message-disposition surface the policy drives, shared by the
201	// modern jetstream.Msg and legacy *nats.Msg adapters so both entry points run
202	// the identical logic.
203	type disposer interface {

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"time"
7	
8		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
9		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
10		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
11		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute"
12		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes"
13		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
14	)
15	
16	// DefaultPublishTimeout bounds the wait for the broker's publish
17	// acknowledgment when a publisher's Timeout is zero. The bound matters because
18	// Entire connections reconnect forever and nats.go buffers publishes while
19	// disconnected: without it, a publisher holding an HTTP request or a message
20	// disposition would wait indefinitely behind an unreachable broker instead
21	// of failing over to its retry path (the caller's outbox, nak, or 5xx).
22	const DefaultPublishTimeout = 5 * time.Second
23	
24	// StartProducerSpan opens a producer span named name on tr, pre-tagged with
25	// the standard messaging attributes (system=nats, operation.type=publish,
26	// destination=subject) — the publish-side counterpart of [StartConsumerSpan].
27	// Extra attrs are appended. The caller owns the span and must End it, and
28	// should Inject the returned ctx into the outgoing message so the consumer can
29	// re-parent.
30	func StartProducerSpan(ctx context.Context, tr trace.Tracer, subject, name string, attrs ...attribute.KeyValue) (context.Context, trace.Span) {
31		base := append([]attribute.KeyValue{
32			attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
33			attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "publish"),
34			attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", subject),
35		}, attrs...)
36		return tr.Start(ctx, name, trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindProducer), trace.WithAttributes(base...)) //nolint:spancheck // the caller owns the span and Ends it
37	}
38	
39	// Publisher is the JetStream publish core shared by Entire's producers on the
40	// modern [jetstream.JetStream] API: a producer span, W3C trace-context
41	// injection, Nats-Msg-Id dedup, and a bounded wait for the broker's ack. Every
42	// service had grown its own copy of exactly this prologue around PublishMsg;
43	// Publisher owns the prologue and nothing else — subject construction, payload
44	// encoding, domain metrics/logging, and the response to a failed publish
45	// (outbox retry, nak, HTTP 5xx) stay with the caller.
46	//
47	// [LegacyPublisher] is the same core for callers still on the legacy
48	// [nats.JetStreamContext] API; it is a transitional bridge — the modern
49	// Publisher is the destination, so a caller migrates by swapping the type and
50	// the LegacyPublisher can be deleted once no caller remains.
51	type Publisher struct {
52		// JS is the JetStream context to publish through.
53		JS jetstream.JetStream
54		// Tracer opens the producer span; nil uses the global OTel tracer
55		// provider.
56		Tracer trace.Tracer
57		// Timeout bounds the wait for the broker's PubAck; 0 uses
58		// DefaultPublishTimeout. It derives from the caller's ctx, so an
59		// already-cancelled ctx still fails fast.
60		Timeout time.Duration
61		// Operation is the caller-selected producer span name (e.g.
62		// "repo.ops.publish"); empty falls back to "publish <subject>". It names the
63		// span only — the messaging operation is recorded as the standard
64		// messaging.operation.type=publish attribute, per OTel semantic conventions,
65		// which reserve messaging.operation.name for the system-specific operation
66		// (send/ack/nack), not an application span name.
67		Operation string
68	}
69	
70	// Publish sends msg and waits — bounded by Timeout — for the broker's ack,
71	// wrapped in a producer span named by Operation (or "publish <subject>" when
72	// unset). A non-empty msgID is set as the Nats-Msg-Id header, the broker-side
73	// dedup key within the stream's duplicate window; empty leaves any Nats-Msg-Id
74	// already on msg untouched. Trace context from ctx is injected into msg's
75	// headers (msg is mutated) so the consumer span re-parents across the hop.
76	//
77	// attrs are the caller's domain span attributes (placement, job identity, …) —
78	// appended to the standard messaging.* set on the producer span. They stay
79	// caller-owned: the shared package does not know them, but records them on the
80	// span it owns so a Phase 3 replacement keeps its existing producer-span tags.
81	//
82	// The returned PubAck reports where the message landed and whether the
83	// broker deduplicated it (PubAck.Duplicate) — a duplicate is a normal
84	// outcome for an at-least-once producer retrying, not an error. The
85	// stream, sequence, and duplicate outcome are also recorded on the span.
86	func (p Publisher) Publish(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg, msgID string, attrs ...attribute.KeyValue) (*jetstream.PubAck, error) {
87		var native *jetstream.PubAck
88		err := publish(ctx, publishConfig{tracer: p.Tracer, operation: p.Operation, timeout: p.Timeout}, msg, msgID, attrs,
89			func(pubCtx context.Context, m *nats.Msg) (ack, error) {
90				pa, perr := p.JS.PublishMsg(pubCtx, m)
91				if perr != nil {
92					return ack{}, perr //nolint:wrapcheck // publish() wraps with the "natsmsg: publish <subject>" prefix
93				}
94				native = pa
95				return ack{stream: pa.Stream, sequence: pa.Sequence, duplicate: pa.Duplicate}, nil
96			})
97		if err != nil {
98			return nil, err
99		}
100		return native, nil
101	}
102	
103	// LegacyJetStream is the subset of the legacy [nats.JetStreamContext] the
104	// [LegacyPublisher] drives — the classic synchronous PublishMsg, satisfied by
105	// nats.JetStreamContext. [DLQPublisher] is an alias of it: dead-lettering and
106	// legacy publishing share the identical publish surface, so a caller can hand
107	// both the one JetStreamContext it already holds.
108	type LegacyJetStream interface {
109		PublishMsg(m *nats.Msg, opts ...nats.PubOpt) (*nats.PubAck, error)
110	}
111	
112	// LegacyPublisher is [Publisher] for callers still on the legacy
113	// [nats.JetStreamContext] API. It shares the identical publish prologue
114	// (producer span, trace-context injection, Nats-Msg-Id, bounded ack, PubAck
115	// telemetry) and differs only in the underlying publish call — legacy
116	// PublishMsg with a nats.Context deadline, versus the modern ctx-native
117	// PublishMsg. It is a transitional bridge: prefer [Publisher] for new code;
118	// this type exists so a legacy caller can adopt go-nuts without first
119	// migrating its JetStream client, and it can be removed once none remain.
120	type LegacyPublisher struct {
121		// JS is the legacy JetStream context to publish through.
122		JS LegacyJetStream
123		// Tracer opens the producer span; nil uses the global OTel tracer
124		// provider.
125		Tracer trace.Tracer
126		// Timeout bounds the wait for the broker's PubAck; 0 uses
127		// DefaultPublishTimeout.
128		Timeout time.Duration
129		// Operation is the caller-selected producer span name (e.g.
130		// "repo.ops.publish"); empty falls back to "publish <subject>". It names the
131		// span only — see [Publisher.Operation].
132		Operation string
133	}
134	
135	// Publish behaves exactly as [Publisher.Publish] — same span, caller attrs,
136	// headers, msg-id, bounded ack, and telemetry — over the legacy
137	// [nats.JetStreamContext] API, returning its native [nats.PubAck].
138	func (p LegacyPublisher) Publish(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg, msgID string, attrs ...attribute.KeyValue) (*nats.PubAck, error) {
139		var native *nats.PubAck
140		err := publish(ctx, publishConfig{tracer: p.Tracer, operation: p.Operation, timeout: p.Timeout}, msg, msgID, attrs,
141			func(pubCtx context.Context, m *nats.Msg) (ack, error) {
142				pa, perr := p.JS.PublishMsg(m, nats.Context(pubCtx))
143				if perr != nil {
144					return ack{}, perr //nolint:wrapcheck // publish() wraps with the "natsmsg: publish <subject>" prefix
145				}
146				native = pa
147				return ack{stream: pa.Stream, sequence: pa.Sequence, duplicate: pa.Duplicate}, nil
148			})
149		if err != nil {
150			return nil, err
151		}
152		return native, nil
153	}
154	
155	// ack is the broker acknowledgment normalized across the legacy nats.PubAck and
156	// modern jetstream.PubAck, carrying just the fields the shared core records on
157	// the producer span.
158	type ack struct {
159		stream    string
160		sequence  uint64
161		duplicate bool
162	}
163	
164	// publishConfig is the publisher configuration the shared core reads,
165	// independent of which JetStream client performs the publish.
166	type publishConfig struct {
167		tracer    trace.Tracer
168		operation string
169		timeout   time.Duration
170	}
171	
172	// publish is the publish prologue shared by [Publisher] and [LegacyPublisher]:
173	// open the producer span (named by cfg.operation or "publish <subject>", tagged
174	// with the caller's attrs alongside the standard messaging.* set), stamp the
175	// Nats-Msg-Id, inject trace context, and bound the ack wait — then run do, the
176	// one step that differs between the modern and legacy clients, and record the
177	// PubAck telemetry (or the error) on the span. do reports the normalized ack and
178	// returns the raw publish error unwrapped so the core can wrap it and callers
179	// can still classify the underlying cause.
180	func publish(ctx context.Context, cfg publishConfig, msg *nats.Msg, msgID string, attrs []attribute.KeyValue, do func(context.Context, *nats.Msg) (ack, error)) error {
181		tr := cfg.tracer
182		if tr == nil {
183			tr = otel.Tracer("github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg")
184		}
185		name := cfg.operation
186		if name == "" {
187			name = "publish " + msg.Subject
188		}
189		ctx, span := StartProducerSpan(ctx, tr, msg.Subject, name, attrs...)
190		defer span.End()
191	
192		if msgID != "" {
193			if msg.Header == nil {
194				msg.Header = nats.Header{}
195			}
196			msg.Header.Set(nats.MsgIdHdr, msgID)
197			span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("messaging.message.id", msgID))
198		}
199		Inject(ctx, msg)
200	
201		timeout := cfg.timeout
202		if timeout == 0 {
203			timeout = DefaultPublishTimeout
204		}
205		pubCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
206		defer cancel()
207	
208		a, err := do(pubCtx, msg)
209		if err != nil {
210			span.RecordError(err)
211			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "publish")
212			return fmt.Errorf("natsmsg: publish %s: %w", msg.Subject, err)
213		}
214		span.SetAttributes(
215			attribute.String("messaging.nats.stream", a.stream),
216			attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", ClampToInt64(a.sequence)),
217			attribute.Bool("messaging.nats.duplicate", a.duplicate),
218		)
219		return nil
220	}

2	// NATS consumers: W3C trace-context propagation over message headers (so a
3	// consumer span parents to the remote producer span and publish → consume
4	// stitches into one trace) and a KeepInProgress heartbeat for long-running
5	// handlers.
6	//
7	// It unifies two service-local copies — entire-core's internal/natsmsg and
8	// entire-api's internal/otelnats (itself ported from mirror-pipeline) — into

23	// HeaderCarrier adapts nats.Header to the OTel TextMapCarrier contract so the
24	// configured propagator can inject/extract traceparent and baggage over a
25	// NATS hop.
26	type HeaderCarrier nats.Header
27	
28	func (c HeaderCarrier) Get(key string) string {
29		v := nats.Header(c).Values(key)
30		if len(v) == 0 {
31			return ""
32		}
33		return v[0]
34	}
35	
36	func (c HeaderCarrier) Set(key, value string) { nats.Header(c).Set(key, value) }
37	
38	// Values returns every value for key, satisfying [propagation.ValuesGetter]:
39	// without it the baggage propagator falls back to Get and reads only the
40	// first of multiple same-named headers, truncating multi-header W3C baggage.
41	func (c HeaderCarrier) Values(key string) []string { return nats.Header(c).Values(key) }
42	
43	func (c HeaderCarrier) Keys() []string {
44		keys := make([]string, 0, len(c))
45		for k := range c {
46			keys = append(keys, k)
47		}
48		return keys
49	}
50	
51	var (
52		_ propagation.TextMapCarrier = HeaderCarrier(nil)
53		_ propagation.ValuesGetter   = HeaderCarrier(nil)
54	)
55	
56	// Inject writes the propagator state from ctx into msg.Header, creating the
57	// header map if absent. Call before publishing so the consumer can re-parent.
58	func Inject(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) {
59		if msg.Header == nil {
60			msg.Header = nats.Header{}
61		}
62		otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Inject(ctx, HeaderCarrier(msg.Header))
63	}
64	
65	// Extract returns ctx with propagator state from msg.Header applied. Call
66	// before starting the consumer span so it parents to the remote producer.
67	func Extract(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) context.Context {
68		return ExtractHeader(ctx, msg.Header)
69	}
70	
71	// ExtractHeader is Extract over a bare nats.Header — it takes the header map
72	// rather than the message so it serves both *nats.Msg (msg.Header) and
73	// jetstream.Msg (msg.Headers()).
74	func ExtractHeader(ctx context.Context, h nats.Header) context.Context {
75		if h == nil {
76			return ctx
77		}
78		return otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Extract(ctx, HeaderCarrier(h))
79	}

81	// Message is the subset of jetstream.Msg the consumer-span helper needs.
82	type Message interface {
83		Headers() nats.Header
84		Subject() string
85	}

87	// StartConsumerSpan extracts the propagated trace context from msg's headers
88	// and opens a consumer span named name on tr, pre-tagged with the standard
89	// messaging attributes (system=nats, destination=subject). Extra attrs are
90	// appended. Collapses the extract+start boilerplate shared by every JetStream
91	// consumer.
92	func StartConsumerSpan(ctx context.Context, tr trace.Tracer, msg Message, name string, attrs ...attribute.KeyValue) (context.Context, trace.Span) {
93		ctx = ExtractHeader(ctx, msg.Headers())

97		}, attrs...)

106		}

1	package natsmsg
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strconv"
7		"time"

9		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
10		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
11	)
12	
13	// dlqPublishTimeout bounds one dead-letter PublishMsg. The consume context has
14	// no deadline, and PublishMsg waits for the PubAck indefinitely; without a
15	// bound a NATS blip would hang the handler (and, since a one-in-flight consumer
16	// keeps a slot occupied, stall the consumer) instead of failing the capture
17	// loudly.
18	const dlqPublishTimeout = 15 * time.Second
19	
20	// DLQ provenance headers added to the captured copy so a replay tool (or a
21	// human) can see why and from where a message was dead-lettered.
22	const (
23		DLQReasonHeader    = "Nats-Dlq-Reason"
24		DLQOriginHeader    = "Nats-Dlq-Origin-Subject"
25		DLQDeliveredHeader = "Nats-Dlq-Delivered"
26		DLQStreamSeqHeader = "Nats-Dlq-Stream-Seq"
27	)
28	
29	// DLQPublisher is the publish surface DeadLetter needs — the legacy
30	// [LegacyJetStream] publish primitive (satisfied by nats.JetStreamContext),
31	// aliased so DeadLetter's signature reads in DLQ terms. Kept minimal so wiring
32	// can hand it the same JetStreamContext the per-cell publishers already hold,
33	// and tests can stub it.
34	type DLQPublisher = LegacyJetStream
35	
36	// SubjectToken sanitizes s into a single valid NATS subject token. NATS tokens
37	// cannot contain spaces, dots, or wildcards, so every character outside
38	// [a-z0-9_-] is replaced with '_' (and letters are lowercased). Use it to turn a
39	// human-readable dead-letter reason ("bad completion payload") into a subject
40	// token ("bad_completion_payload") — publishing to an unsanitized reason would
41	// fail, so the caller would never Ack the poison off a WorkQueue.
42	func SubjectToken(s string) string {
43		// Iterate bytes, not runes: we only keep ASCII [a-z0-9_-] and map everything
44		// else (including every byte of a multi-byte rune) to '_', so a byte loop is
45		// both correct and free of a rune->byte narrowing conversion.
46		b := make([]byte, 0, len(s))
47		for i := range len(s) {
48			c := s[i]
49			switch {
50			case c >= 'a' && c <= 'z', c >= '0' && c <= '9', c == '_', c == '-':
51				b = append(b, c)
52			case c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z':
53				b = append(b, c-'A'+'a')
54			default:
55				b = append(b, '_')
56			}
57		}
58		if len(b) == 0 {
59			return "unknown"
60		}
61		return string(b)
62	}
63	
64	// DeadLetter republishes a poison message to dlqSubject, preserving its payload
65	// and headers and adding Nats-Dlq-* provenance (reason, origin subject,
66	// delivery count, stream sequence).
67	//
68	// It is the capture step a consumer runs before giving up on a message it can
69	// never process. DeadLetter copies the poison to a durable DLQ subject so it can
70	// be inspected or replayed, and the caller then removes the original from the
71	// stream — a Term on the final delivery (see backoff.Policy.TermOnExhaustion,
72	// whose doc notes callers "DLQ capture before calling NakOrTerm") or a plain
73	// Ack. Without this step a Term'd or MaxDeliver-exhausted message is discarded
74	// with no trail; DeadLetter is what makes the give-up auditable and recoverable.
75	//
76	// Returns an error if the republish fails; on error the caller MUST NOT remove
77	// the original — Nak or leave it so the poison is never dropped without a
78	// captured copy. Publishing is bounded by dlqPublishTimeout regardless of ctx's
79	// deadline.
80	func DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, pub DLQPublisher, dlqSubject string, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) error {
81		hdr := nats.Header{}
82		for k, v := range msg.Headers() {
83			hdr[k] = append([]string(nil), v...)
84		}
85		hdr.Set(DLQReasonHeader, reason)
86		hdr.Set(DLQOriginHeader, msg.Subject())
87		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
88			hdr.Set(DLQDeliveredHeader, strconv.FormatUint(meta.NumDelivered, 10))
89			hdr.Set(DLQStreamSeqHeader, strconv.FormatUint(meta.Sequence.Stream, 10))
90		}
91	
92		out := &nats.Msg{Subject: dlqSubject, Data: msg.Data(), Header: hdr}
93	
94		pubCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, dlqPublishTimeout)
95		defer cancel()
96		if _, err := pub.PublishMsg(out, nats.Context(pubCtx)); err != nil {
97			return fmt.Errorf("dead-letter publish to %q: %w", dlqSubject, err)
98		}
99		return nil
100	}

41	const (
42		// DefaultAckWait is how long JetStream waits for an ack before redelivery
43		// when Config.AckWait is zero — comfortably longer than an RPC round-trip
44		// plus a DB upsert, short enough that a stuck message redelivers promptly.
45		DefaultAckWait = 30 * time.Second
46		// DefaultMaxDeliver caps redelivery before JetStream stops redelivering a
47		// message when Config.MaxDeliver is zero.

51	// Config describes the durable consumer to create and how to trace/log it. The
52	// filter is given as either FilterSubject (single) or FilterSubjects (multi),
53	// mirroring jetstream.ConsumerConfig, so a migrated consumer preserves its
54	// existing on-server filter form exactly.
55	type Config struct {
56		Stream         string        // JetStream stream to bind (must already exist)
57		Durable        string        // durable consumer name, stable across restarts
58		FilterSubject  string        // set this OR FilterSubjects
59		FilterSubjects []string      // set this OR FilterSubject
60		AckWait        time.Duration // 0 → DefaultAckWait (see EffectiveAckWait)
61		MaxDeliver     int           // 0 → DefaultMaxDeliver (see EffectiveMaxDeliver)
62		SpanName       string        // per-message consumer span name (e.g. "repolifecycle.consume")
63		Name           string        // short consumer name, used as the log prefix
64	
65		// InactiveThreshold mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.InactiveThreshold:
66		// how long the durable may go without an active subscription before the
67		// server deletes it; zero means never (the JetStream default for
68		// durables). Consumers on interest-retention streams set this so a
69		// decommissioned durable stops pinning every message it would have
70		// received, instead of holding them until the stream's MaxAge.
71		InactiveThreshold time.Duration
72	
73		// MaxAckPending mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxAckPending: the
74		// server-side cap on deliveries outstanding un-acked across ALL replicas
75		// sharing the durable; zero uses the server default (1000). Distinct
76		// from MaxMessages below, which caps only this process's client-side
77		// buffer.
78		MaxAckPending int
79	
80		// Tracer opens the per-message consumer span; nil uses the global OTel
81		// tracer provider.
82		Tracer trace.Tracer
83		// Logger receives the scaffold's own log lines (decode-term warnings,
84		// consume errors); nil uses slog.Default.
85		Logger *slog.Logger
86	
87		// KeepInProgress runs a natsmsg.KeepInProgress heartbeat while handle
88		// executes, for handlers that legitimately outrun AckWait. The extension
89		// is capped, so a wedged handler still redelivers — see
90		// natsmsg.KeepInProgress. The heartbeat stops when handle returns; a tick
91		// racing the handler's own terminal Ack/Nak/Term is a client-side no-op
92		// (nats.go marks the message disposed locally) that halts the heartbeat.
93		//
94		// Setting this forces the prefetch to one message (see MaxMessages): the
95		// heartbeat extends only the delivery the handler holds, so anything
96		// buffered behind a long handler would exhaust its AckWait unextended.
97		KeepInProgress bool
98	
99		// MaxMessages caps how many deliveries the consume loop buffers
100		// client-side (jetstream.PullMaxMessages); 0 uses the nats.go default
101		// (500). AckWait runs from server delivery into that buffer, not from
102		// callback dispatch, and callbacks run serially — so a consumer whose
103		// handler can approach AckWait should keep this small or queued
104		// deliveries expire and redeliver concurrently to other replicas.
105		// KeepInProgress forces it to 1; setting both to conflicting values is a
106		// Start error.
107		MaxMessages int
108	}
109	
110	// EffectiveAckWait is the AckWait actually applied to the JetStream consumer:
111	// Config.AckWait, or DefaultAckWait when zero. Use it — not the raw field —
112	// anywhere the real value matters, e.g. wiring a natsmsg.KeepInProgress
113	// heartbeat by hand (a zero ackWait there is a no-op).
114	func (c Config) EffectiveAckWait() time.Duration {
115		if c.AckWait == 0 {
116			return DefaultAckWait
117		}
118		return c.AckWait
119	}
120	
121	// EffectiveMaxDeliver is the MaxDeliver actually applied to the JetStream
122	// consumer: Config.MaxDeliver, or DefaultMaxDeliver when zero. Use it — not
123	// the raw field — when building a backoff.Policy for this consumer's
124	// messages: the two packages read zero differently (here it means "default
125	// to DefaultMaxDeliver"; on the policy it means unlimited redeliveries, the
126	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig semantics), so passing a zero Config.MaxDeliver
127	// through verbatim would make TermOnExhaustion never fire on the broker's
128	// real final delivery and orphan work-queue messages (COR-762).
129	func (c Config) EffectiveMaxDeliver() int {
130		if c.MaxDeliver == 0 {
131			return DefaultMaxDeliver
132		}
133		return c.MaxDeliver
134	}

136	// validate rejects the configuration errors no retry can fix; shared by
137	// [Start] (one-shot) and [Run] (supervised, which must fail fast on these
138	// rather than retry them forever).
139	func (c Config) validate(nc *nats.Conn, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
140		if c.KeepInProgress && c.MaxMessages > 1 {
141			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): KeepInProgress requires MaxMessages <= 1: the heartbeat extends only the in-flight delivery, so %d buffered messages would exhaust AckWait behind a long handler", c.Name, c.MaxMessages)
142		}
143		if c.Stream == "" {
144			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Stream is required", c.Name)
145		}
146		if c.Durable == "" {
147			// CreateOrUpdateConsumer accepts an empty durable and silently makes
148			// an ephemeral, server-named consumer — losing the stable
149			// resume-across-restarts behavior this scaffold promises.
150			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Durable is required", c.Name)
151		}
152		if onMsg == nil {
153			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): onMsg is required", c.Name)
154		}
155		if c.FilterSubject != "" && len(c.FilterSubjects) != 0 {
156			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): set FilterSubject or FilterSubjects, not both", c.Name)
157		}
158		for i, subject := range c.FilterSubjects {
159			if subject == "" {
160				return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): FilterSubjects[%d] is empty", c.Name, i)
161			}
162		}
163		if c.AckWait < 0 {
164			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): AckWait must not be negative", c.Name)
165		}
166		if c.MaxDeliver < -1 {
167			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxDeliver must be -1 (unlimited), 0 (default), or positive", c.Name)
168		}
169		if c.MaxMessages < 0 {
170			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxMessages must not be negative", c.Name)
171		}
172		if c.MaxAckPending < -1 {
173			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxAckPending must be -1 (unlimited), 0 (server default), or positive", c.Name)
174		}
175		if c.InactiveThreshold < 0 {
176			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): InactiveThreshold must not be negative", c.Name)
177		}
178		if nc == nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): nil nats conn", c.Name)
180		}
181		return nil
182	}

184	func (c Config) tracer() trace.Tracer {
185		if c.Tracer == nil {
186			return otel.Tracer("github.com/entireio/go-nuts/jsconsumer")
187		}
188		return c.Tracer
189	}
190	
191	func (c Config) logger() *slog.Logger {
192		if c.Logger == nil {
193			return slog.Default()
194		}
195		return c.Logger
196	}
197	
198	// isShutdownConsumeErr reports whether a consume error is the benign result
199	// of the connection going away during shutdown. [nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]
200	// covers the core nats.go sentinels, but the jetstream consume loop surfaces
201	// its OWN [jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed] — a distinct value that wraps
202	// neither — so it must be matched separately or a clean rollout drain still
203	// logs a warning (the COR-923 noise this suppression exists to remove). As
204	// with the root classifier, it is only "clean" when ctx is already done; a
205	// mid-run connection loss is a genuine fault worth logging.
206	func isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx context.Context, err error) bool {
207		return nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) ||
208			(ctx.Err() != nil && errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed))
209	}
210	
211	// Runner is a live consume loop. Stop halts it and is idempotent.
212	type Runner struct {
213		cc jetstream.ConsumeContext
214		// closed is cc.Closed(), captured while the subscription is live (the
215		// same channel is returned on every call, so capturing once avoids any
216		// post-Stop race) — it closes when the consume loop has fully wound
217		// down, including an in-flight handler.
218		closed <-chan struct{}
219		// watcherDone closes when Start's context-cancellation watcher exits. It is
220		// intentionally internal: callers synchronize on Stop, while tests pin that
221		// an explicit Stop does not retain a goroutine until the parent context ends.
222		watcherDone <-chan struct{}
223		stop        sync.Once
224	}
225	
226	// Stop halts the consume loop and blocks until it has fully wound down —
227	// including an in-flight handler — so a caller may tear down what handlers
228	// use (stores, publishers, the NATS connection) the moment it returns: the
229	// cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering (COR-923). Safe on a nil or
230	// never-Started Runner, idempotent, and safe for concurrent use — an
231	// explicit Stop can race the context-cancel stop armed by Start. Must not be
232	// called from inside the handler; it would deadlock waiting on itself.
233	func (r *Runner) Stop() {
234		if r == nil || r.cc == nil {
235			return
236		}
237		r.stop.Do(r.cc.Stop)
238		<-r.closed
239	}
240	
241	// Start creates/updates the durable consumer on nc and begins delivering
242	// messages to onMsg, returning a Runner that Stops when ctx is cancelled. The
243	// stream must already exist (provisioned declaratively); callers whose cells
244	// opt in per-stream gate Start behind that opt-in so a cell without the stream
245	// doesn't error at CreateOrUpdateConsumer.
246	//
247	// Consume errors are logged at Warn, except a drain/close during shutdown —
248	// both the core nats.go sentinels ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]) and jetstream's
249	// own connection-closed error — which is a clean exit rather than a fault.
250	func Start(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) (*Runner, error) {
251		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
252			return nil, err
253		}
254		js, err := jetstream.New(nc)
255		if err != nil {
256			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): jetstream.New: %w", cfg.Name, err)
257		}
258		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, cfg.Stream, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
259			Durable:           cfg.Durable,
260			AckPolicy:         jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
261			AckWait:           cfg.EffectiveAckWait(),
262			MaxDeliver:        cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(),
263			FilterSubject:     cfg.FilterSubject,
264			FilterSubjects:    cfg.FilterSubjects,
265			InactiveThreshold: cfg.InactiveThreshold,
266			MaxAckPending:     cfg.MaxAckPending,
267		})
268		if err != nil {
269			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): create consumer %s/%s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, cfg.Durable, err)
270		}
271		consumeOpts := []jetstream.PullConsumeOpt{jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {
272			if isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx, cerr) {
273				return
274			}
275			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume error", slog.Any("error", cerr))
276		})}
277		switch {
278		case cfg.KeepInProgress:
279			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(1))
280		case cfg.MaxMessages > 0:
281			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(cfg.MaxMessages))
282		}
283		cc, err := cons.Consume(onMsg, consumeOpts...)
284		if err != nil {
285			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): consume %s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, err)
286		}
287		watcherDone := make(chan struct{})
288		r := &Runner{cc: cc, closed: cc.Closed(), watcherDone: watcherDone}
289		go func() {
290			defer close(watcherDone)
291			select {
292			case <-ctx.Done():
293				r.Stop()
294			case <-r.closed:
295			}
296		}()
297		return r, nil
298	}
299	
300	// isRetryableStartError classifies the narrow set of failures that can become
301	// healthy without changing Config or replacing nc. Everything else returns to
302	// the owner so a bad deployment cannot stay alive indefinitely with no
303	// consumer. Unknown server-side 5xx responses are retried, except known
304	// permanent JetStream configuration/account errors whose API happens to use a
305	// 5xx status.
306	func isRetryableStartError(err error) bool {
307		if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) ||
308			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrNoResponders) ||
309			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) ||
310			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrDisconnected) {
311			return true
312		}
313	
314		var jsErr jetstream.JetStreamError
315		if !errors.As(err, &jsErr) || jsErr.APIError() == nil {
316			return false
317		}
318		apiErr := jsErr.APIError()
319		switch apiErr.ErrorCode { //nolint:exhaustive // unrecognized 5xx codes are deliberately retryable; all other unknown codes fail closed
320		case jetstream.JSErrCodeBadRequest,
321			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerCreate,
322			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerNameExists,
323			jetstream.JSErrCodeMaximumConsumersLimit,
324			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabledForAccount,
325			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabled,
326			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerAlreadyExists,
327			jetstream.JSErrCodeDuplicateFilterSubjects,
328			jetstream.JSErrCodeOverlappingFilterSubjects,
329			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerEmptyFilter,
330			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerExists:
331			return false
332		default:
333			return apiErr.Code >= 500
334		}
335	}
336	
337	// Retry envelope for [Run]'s supervision: exponential from runRetryInitial
338	// doubling to runRetryMax, reset once a consume loop survives longer than the
339	// max. Package vars (not consts) so tests can compress the schedule.
340	var (
341		runRetryInitial = time.Second
342		runRetryMax     = 30 * time.Second
343	)
344	
345	// Run supervises the consume loop [Start] builds. Where Start is one-shot —
346	// an error at consumer creation is returned, and a consume loop that closes
347	// underneath the caller (consumer deleted on the server, subscription
348	// invalidated) stays closed — Run retries both with exponential backoff
349	// (runRetryInitial doubling to runRetryMax, reset after a loop that outlives
350	// the max). In particular a stream that is not provisioned yet at boot — the
351	// declarative-provisioning race — is a retry, not a crash.
352	//
353	// Run blocks until ctx is cancelled, then joins the live loop (including an
354	// in-flight handler, see [Runner.Stop]) before returning, so it composes with
355	// the cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering as the body of a supervised
356	// goroutine:
357	//
358	//	g.Go(func(ctx context.Context) {
359	//		if err := jsconsumer.Run(ctx, nc, cfg, onMsg); err != nil {
360	//			log.Error("consumer config rejected", "error", err)
361	//		}
362	//	})
363	//
364	// Local configuration errors and permanent server responses (invalid consumer
365	// configuration, authorization/account setup) can never succeed on retry and
366	// are returned immediately. A missing declarative stream, temporary transport
367	// failure, or unknown server-side 5xx response remains supervised. A nil return
368	// means a clean, ctx-driven exit.
369	func Run(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
370		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
371			return err
372		}
373		delay := runRetryInitial
374		for {
375			// Each attempt gets a child context so the cancel-watcher goroutine
376			// Start arms is released when the attempt dies, instead of one
377			// accumulating per recreate for the life of the process.
378			attemptCtx, cancelAttempt := context.WithCancel(ctx)
379			r, err := Start(attemptCtx, nc, cfg, onMsg)
380			if err != nil {
381				cancelAttempt()
382				if ctx.Err() != nil {
383					return nil //nolint:nilerr // a Start error during shutdown is a clean, ctx-driven exit, not a fault to report
384				}
385				if !isRetryableStartError(err) {
386					return err
387				}
388				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": start consumer failed; retrying",
389					slog.Any("error", err), slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
390			} else {
391				started := time.Now()
392				select {
393				case <-ctx.Done():
394					r.Stop()
395					cancelAttempt()
396					return nil
397				case <-r.closed:
398					cancelAttempt()
399					if ctx.Err() != nil {
400						return nil //nolint:nilerr // the loop closing during shutdown is the expected wind-down, not a fault
401					}
402					// A loop that ran long enough to be called healthy earns a
403					// fresh envelope; a flapping one keeps escalating.
404					if time.Since(started) >= runRetryMax {
405						delay = runRetryInitial
406					}
407					cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume loop closed; recreating",
408						slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
409				}
410			}
411			select {
412			case <-ctx.Done():
413				return nil
414			case <-time.After(delay):
415			}
416			delay = min(delay*2, runRetryMax)
417		}
418	}
419	
420	// Process runs the per-message prologue shared by every consumer: open the
421	// consumer span (re-parented to the producer across the NATS hop), decode the
422	// payload, and on a decode error record it, log "<Name>: decode <Stream>;
423	// term", invoke onUndecodable (so the caller bumps its own drop metric with
424	// its own attributes), and Term the message — a poison payload won't decode on
425	// redelivery. On success it invokes handle with the span-enriched context, the
426	// live span (for RecordError/SetStatus on the business error paths), the
427	// message, and the decoded event; with Config.KeepInProgress set, an AckWait
428	// heartbeat runs for the duration of handle.
429	//
430	// Callers wire Process as the func they pass to Start AND the entry point
431	// their tests drive, so the decode-or-term path is exercised the same way in
432	// production and tests.
433	func Process[E any](
434		ctx context.Context,
435		msg jetstream.Msg,
436		cfg Config,
437		decode func([]byte) (E, error),
438		handle func(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, ev E),
439		onUndecodable func(ctx context.Context),
440	) {
441		ctx, span := natsmsg.StartConsumerSpan(ctx, cfg.tracer(), msg, cfg.SpanName)
442		defer span.End()
443	
444		ev, err := decode(msg.Data())
445		if err != nil {
446			span.RecordError(err)
447			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "decode")
448			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": decode "+cfg.Stream+"; term",
449				slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
450			if onUndecodable != nil {
451				onUndecodable(ctx)
452			}
453			if termErr := msg.Term(); termErr != nil {
454				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": term failed", slog.Any("error", termErr))
455			}
456			return
457		}
458		if cfg.KeepInProgress {
459			stop := natsmsg.KeepInProgress(msg.InProgress, cfg.EffectiveAckWait())
460			defer stop()
461		}
462		handle(ctx, span, msg, ev)
463	}

## 3. `internal/natspub` — full inventory (`internal/natspub/natspub.go`, 131 lines)

Purpose: the shared JetStream publish core behind all typed job/event publishers — one producer span, dedup header, bounded pub-ack wait, one INFO log. This is what the ticket wants routed through `natsmsg`'s "shared legacy publishing adapter."

Exported API:
- **`const MsgIDHeader = "Nats-Msg-Id"`** (`:26`) — JetStream dedup header.
- **`const AckWait = 5 * time.Second`** (`:35`) — bounds the synchronous pub-ack wait (see doc `:27-34`: converts a reconnect stall into a caller error → Nak → redelivery).
- **`type JetStreamPublisher interface { PublishMsg(*nats.Msg, ...nats.PubOpt) (*nats.PubAck, error) }`** (`:38`) — the publish subset of `nats.JetStreamContext`.
- **`type Publication struct`** (`:44`) — fields: `Tracer`, `SpanName`, `ErrKind`, `LogMsg`, `Subject`, `MsgID`, `Marshal func() ([]byte, error)`, `SpanAttrs []attribute.KeyValue`, `LogAttrs []slog.Attr`.
- **`func PlacementAttrs(jurisdiction, cluster string) []attribute.KeyValue`** (`:72`) — standard `entire.target_jurisdiction` / `entire.target_cluster_id` attrs.
- **`func Publish(ctx, js JetStreamPublisher, pub Publication) error`** (`:80`) — the core.

What `Publish` does (span naming, msg-id, PubAck, timeouts):
- Starts a **producer span** `pub.SpanName` from `otel.Tracer(pub.Tracer)` with `SpanKindProducer` (`:87-90`). Standard attrs `messaging.system=nats`, `messaging.operation.type=publish`, `messaging.destination.name=<subject>` then domain `SpanAttrs`.

- Builds `*nats.Msg`, sets `Nats-Msg-Id` header = `pub.MsgID`, calls **`otelnats.Inject(ctx, msg)`** (`:100-106`), sets `messaging.message.id` attr.
- **Bounded pub-ack:** `context.WithTimeout(ctx, AckWait)` then `js.PublishMsg(msg, nats.Context(pubCtx))` (`:109-111`).
- On publish error: `RecordError` + `SetStatus(Error, "nats publish")`, returns `fmt.Errorf("publish %s: %w", ...)` (`:112-116`).
- On success: sets `messaging.nats.sequence` (from `ack.Sequence`) and `messaging.nats.duplicate` (from `ack.Duplicate`) span attrs (`:118-121`), and logs one INFO with `LogAttrs` + `subject`/`msg_id`/`sequence`/`duplicate` (`:123-129`).

67		// maxAge/maxBytes wall, which stalled the whole mirror pipeline on
68		// 2026-06-01. 72h sits under the stream's 96h maxAge.
69		//
70		// Tension with defaultMaxDeliver = -1, acknowledged: this consumer's
71		// events are not re-derivable, and a deployment down for more than 72h
72		// loses the durable and with it the events published until it returns.
73		// That is a disaster-recovery scenario (entire-core-global absent for
74		// three days); the perms reconciler CronJob is the authoritative
75		// backstop that re-derives grant state from SpiceDB + GitHub, and an
76		// unblocked webhook pipeline for every other consumer is worth more
77		// than a >72h-stale cursor.
78		defaultInactiveThreshold = 72 * time.Hour
79	)

81	const tracerName = "permswebhook"

83	// eventApplier turns a decoded webhook into DB writes. The metadata path
84	// (applier) and the read-model path (permsApplier) both satisfy it, so the
85	// Consumer's handle/ack loop is shared between the two durables.
86	type eventApplier interface {
87		apply(ctx context.Context, event, deliveryID string, observedAt time.Time, body []byte) error
88	}

90	// Config holds the consumer's required and tunable inputs. Zero values
91	// fall back to the package-level defaults.
92	type Config struct {
93		Service     *githubperms.Service
94		Conn        *nats.Conn
95		DurableName string
96		// Applier and FilterSubjects select what this consumer does. Zero
97		// values default to the metadata path (the applier built from Service,
98		// filtering the three installation/repo subjects) so existing callers
99		// are unchanged; the read-model consumer passes its own.
100		Applier        eventApplier
101		FilterSubjects []string
102		// Visibility propagates repository public/private changes to SpiceDB on
103		// every repository upsert (COR-758). Optional: nil disables propagation
104		// (tests / deployments that don't have SpiceDB wired).
105		Visibility visibilityPropagator
106		// Ops fans repo-operation jobs out around the metadata writes:
107		// teardown on the permanent delete, suspend on the reversible
108		// offline events, resume on re-attach. Optional: nil leaves the
109		// consumer metadata-only, used in deployments without repo-ops
110		// wiring. Only consulted for the default metadata applier (when
111		// Applier is nil); the read-model applier publishes no ops.
112		Ops opsFanout
113		// Sweep publishes one immediate perms-sweep job after a successful
114		// installation.created / installation_repositories.added upsert, so a
115		// fresh install's collaborator snapshots start within seconds instead of
116		// at the next hourly enumerator tick. Optional and best-effort: nil (or
117		// a publish failure) leaves the hourly enumerator as the only trigger.
118		// Only consulted for the default metadata applier.
119		Sweep             sweepPublisher
120		AckWait           time.Duration
121		MaxDeliver        int
122		NakDelay          time.Duration
123		FetchBatch        int
124		RetryBackoffMx    time.Duration
125		InactiveThreshold time.Duration
126	}

128	// Consumer is the long-running JetStream subscriber that drains a filtered
129	// set of webhook event subjects off webhooks_github_v1 and applies them.
130	type Consumer struct {
131		cfg     Config
132		applier eventApplier
133	}
134	
135	// New validates the config and returns a Consumer. Fails fast if required
136	// deps are nil so the wiring layer surfaces the problem at startup rather
137	// than at first message.
138	func New(cfg Config) (*Consumer, error) {
139		if cfg.Conn == nil {
140			return nil, errors.New("permswebhook: Conn is required")
141		}
142		if cfg.Applier == nil {
143			// Default: the installation/repo metadata path. It needs the
144			// metadata Service.
145			if cfg.Service == nil {
146				return nil, errors.New("permswebhook: Service is required for the default metadata applier")
147			}
148			cfg.Applier = &applier{svc: cfg.Service, visibility: cfg.Visibility, ops: cfg.Ops, sweep: cfg.Sweep}
149		}
150		if len(cfg.FilterSubjects) == 0 {
151			cfg.FilterSubjects = filterSubjects
152		}
153		if cfg.DurableName == "" {
154			cfg.DurableName = DurableName
155		}
156		if cfg.AckWait == 0 {
157			cfg.AckWait = defaultAckWait
158		}
159		if cfg.MaxDeliver == 0 {
160			cfg.MaxDeliver = defaultMaxDeliver
161		}
162		if cfg.NakDelay == 0 {
163			cfg.NakDelay = defaultNakDelay
164		}
165		if cfg.FetchBatch == 0 {
166			cfg.FetchBatch = defaultFetchBatch
167		}
168		if cfg.RetryBackoffMx == 0 {
169			cfg.RetryBackoffMx = defaultRetryBackoffMax
170		}
171		if cfg.InactiveThreshold == 0 {
172			cfg.InactiveThreshold = defaultInactiveThreshold
173		}
174		return &Consumer{cfg: cfg, applier: cfg.Applier}, nil
175	}
176	
177	// consumerConfig is the durable pull-consumer contract Run create-or-updates and
178	// consumes from. webhooks_github_v1 is operator-owned; this consumer binds its
179	// own durable + multi-filter on it. InactiveThreshold rides the create-or-update
180	// config, which applies the full config on every call, so the reap window is
181	// reconciled in place with no separate step.
182	func (c *Consumer) consumerConfig() jsconsumer.Config {
183		return jsconsumer.Config{
184			Name:              "webhook-perms",
185			Stream:            StreamName,
186			Durable:           c.cfg.DurableName,
187			FilterSubjects:    c.cfg.FilterSubjects,
188			AckWait:           c.cfg.AckWait,
189			MaxDeliver:        c.cfg.MaxDeliver,
190			InactiveThreshold: c.cfg.InactiveThreshold,
191			MaxMessages:       c.cfg.FetchBatch,
192		}
193	}
194	
195	// Run supervises the webhook-perms durable until ctx is cancelled. The
196	// create-or-update / consume / reconnect-with-backoff mechanism lives in
197	// go-nuts/jsconsumer; handling and disposition stay here (see handleMessage).
198	// InactiveThreshold rides consumerConfig, which the runner re-applies on every
199	// create-or-update, so the reap window is reconciled in place with no separate
200	// step. jsconsumer.Run blocks until ctx is cancelled.
201	func (c *Consumer) Run(ctx context.Context) {
202		if err := jsconsumer.Run(ctx, c.cfg.Conn, c.consumerConfig(), func(msg jetstream.Msg) {
203			c.handleMessage(ctx, msg)
204		}); err != nil {
205			slogutil.Error(ctx, "webhook-perms consumer stopped", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
206		}
207	}
208	
209	// handleMessage processes one delivery and applies a disposition
210	// (Ack / Nak / Term). Span and log records cover every outcome.
211	func (c *Consumer) handleMessage(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg) {
212		ctx = natsmsg.ExtractHeader(ctx, msg.Headers())
213		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(tracerName).Start(ctx, "mirror.perms.webhook.consume",
214			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindConsumer),
215			trace.WithAttributes(
216				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
217				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "receive"),
218				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", msg.Subject()),
219			),
220		)
221		defer span.End()
222	
223		// Poison-message guard: a panic while decoding or applying one delivery must
224		// not kill the consumer goroutine. A redelivering poison event (e.g. the
225		// COR-730 membership event that nil-derefed a.mirrors) would otherwise crash
226		// entire-core on every restart. Recover, record the stack at ERROR, and
227		// Term the delivery so it does not redeliver forever. Both the metadata and
228		// read-model durables share this loop, so both are protected.
229		defer func() {
230			if r := recover(); r != nil {
231				c.recoverPanic(ctx, span, msg, r)
232			}
233		}()
234	
235		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil {
236			span.SetAttributes(
237				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", natsmsg.ClampToInt64(meta.Sequence.Stream)),
238				attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.delivery_count", natsmsg.ClampToInt64(meta.NumDelivered)),
239			)
240		}
241	
242		fw, err := unmarshalEnvelope(msg.Data())
243		if err != nil {
244			c.terminate(ctx, span, msg, "bad envelope", err)
245			return
246		}
247		span.SetAttributes(
248			attribute.String("entire.webhook.event", fw.Event),
249			attribute.String("entire.webhook.delivery_id", fw.DeliveryID),
250		)
251	
252		slogutil.Info(ctx, "webhook-perms consume",
253			slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()),
254			slog.String("event", fw.Event),
255			slog.String("delivery_id", fw.DeliveryID),
256		)
257	
258		// Keep the delivery alive while apply runs: a whole-installation
259		// teardown fan-out publishes one job per placement and can legitimately
260		// outlive AckWait on a large installation — without the heartbeat the
261		// broker would redeliver the SAME event into a second concurrent
262		// fan-out, and an apply that consistently exceeds AckWait would
263		// redeliver forever without ever Acking. The extension is capped
264		// (natsmsg.KeepInProgress) so a truly wedged apply still falls back to
265		// AckWait redelivery on a healthy replica. Stopped (idempotently)
266		// before every terminal disposition; the deferred stop covers the
267		// panic path, where recoverPanic Terms.
268		stopHeartbeat := natsmsg.KeepInProgress(func() error { return msg.InProgress() }, c.cfg.AckWait)
269		defer stopHeartbeat()
270	
271		applyErr := c.applier.apply(ctx, fw.Event, fw.DeliveryID, fw.ReceivedAt, fw.Body)
272		stopHeartbeat()
273		if applyErr != nil {
274			c.disposeError(ctx, span, msg, applyErr)
275			return
276		}
277		if err := msg.Ack(); err != nil {
278			slogutil.Warn(ctx, "webhook-perms ack failed", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
279		}
280	}
281	
282	// terminate logs + spans the failure and Term()s the message so it won't
283	// be redelivered. Reserved for structurally broken inputs — no amount of
284	// retrying will make them apply.
285	func (c *Consumer) terminate(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string, err error) {
286		span.RecordError(err)
287		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, reason)
288		span.SetAttributes(
289			attribute.Bool("entire.error.permanent", true),
290			attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true),
291		)
292		slogutil.Error(ctx, "webhook-perms terminating message",
293			slog.String("reason", reason),
294			slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()),
295			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
296		)
297		if termErr := msg.Term(); termErr != nil {
298			slogutil.Warn(ctx, "webhook-perms term failed", slog.String("error", termErr.Error()))
299		}
300	}
301	
302	// recoverPanic disposes of a message whose processing panicked. It logs the
303	// recovered value plus a stack at ERROR and Term()s the delivery so a poison
304	// event can't redeliver forever (one bad event => one ERROR log, not a global
305	// outage). The panic is treated as permanent — a nil-deref or bad-shape crash
306	// won't fix itself on replay.
307	func (c *Consumer) recoverPanic(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, recovered any) {
308		err := fmt.Errorf("panic: %v", recovered)
309		span.RecordError(err)
310		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "panic")
311		span.SetAttributes(
312			attribute.Bool("entire.error.permanent", true),
313			attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true),
314		)
315		slogutil.Error(ctx, "webhook-perms recovered panic; terminating message",
316			slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()),
317			slog.Any("panic", recovered),
318			slog.String("stack", string(debug.Stack())),
319		)
320		if termErr := msg.Term(); termErr != nil {
321			slogutil.Warn(ctx, "webhook-perms term after panic failed", slog.String("error", termErr.Error()))
322		}
323	}
324	
325	// disposeError chooses Term vs Nak for an apply-time failure. Permanent
326	// errors (malformed body) Term so they don't burn the redelivery budget;
327	// transient errors (DB blip) Nak with delay so they reapply after backoff.
328	func (c *Consumer) disposeError(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, err error) {
329		span.RecordError(err)
330		if isPermanent(err) {
331			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "permanent")
332			span.SetAttributes(
333				attribute.Bool("entire.error.permanent", true),
334				attribute.Bool("entire.message.terminated", true),
335			)
336			slogutil.Error(ctx, "webhook-perms apply permanent failure",
337				slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()),
338				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
339			)
340			if termErr := msg.Term(); termErr != nil {
341				slogutil.Warn(ctx, "webhook-perms term failed", slog.String("error", termErr.Error()))
342			}
343			return
344		}
345		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "retriable")
346		span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.error.permanent", false))
347		delay := c.nakDelay(deliveryCount(msg))
348		slogutil.Warn(ctx, "webhook-perms apply retriable failure",
349			slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()),
350			slog.Duration("retry_in", delay),
351			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
352		)
353		if nakErr := msg.NakWithDelay(delay); nakErr != nil {
354			slogutil.Warn(ctx, "webhook-perms nak failed", slog.String("error", nakErr.Error()))
355		}
356	}
357	
358	// nakDelay grows the redelivery delay geometrically with the delivery count,
359	// from NakDelay up to RetryBackoffMx — mirroring repoops' backoff. MaxDeliver
360	// is unlimited, so without it a message stuck behind a persistent transient
361	// failure would redeliver every NakDelay for hours and hammer a store that is
362	// trying to recover.
363	func (c *Consumer) nakDelay(numDelivered uint64) time.Duration {
364		if numDelivered <= 1 {
365			return c.cfg.NakDelay
366		}
367		shift := numDelivered - 1
368		if shift >= 63 {
369			return c.cfg.RetryBackoffMx
370		}
371		d := c.cfg.NakDelay << shift
372		if d <= 0 { // overflow past the int64 Duration range
373			return c.cfg.RetryBackoffMx
374		}
375		return min(d, c.cfg.RetryBackoffMx)
376	}
377	
378	// deliveryCount is the message's NumDelivered (1 on first delivery), or 1 when
379	// metadata is unavailable (e.g. a non-JetStream test message) so the backoff
380	// degrades to the base NakDelay rather than panicking.
381	func deliveryCount(msg jetstream.Msg) uint64 {
382		meta, err := msg.Metadata()
383		if err != nil || meta == nil {
384			return 1
385		}
386		return meta.NumDelivered
387	}
388	
389	// permanentError marks an error as non-retriable so the disposition
390	// chooses Term instead of Nak.
391	type permanentError struct{ err error }
392	
393	func (e *permanentError) Error() string { return e.err.Error() }
394	func (e *permanentError) Unwrap() error { return e.err }
395	
396	func permanent(err error) error { return &permanentError{err: err} }
397	
398	func isPermanent(err error) bool {
399		var pe *permanentError
400		return errors.As(err, &pe)
401	}

20	
21	// NatsMsgIDHeader is the JetStream dedup header. A re-published job for
22	// the same op, placement, and observation within StreamDuplicatesWindow
23	// collapses server-side, so the producer can retry one webhook without
24	// enqueuing it twice. Distinct observations must not collapse: an upstream
25	// can be removed, re-added, then removed again inside the duplicate
26	// window, and the older job may legitimately skip via the
27	// last-writer-wins gate.
28	const NatsMsgIDHeader = "Nats-Msg-Id"
29	
30	// JetStreamPublisher is the slice of nats.JetStreamContext the Publisher
31	// needs, pulled out so tests can stub publish without a live JetStream.
32	type JetStreamPublisher interface {
33		PublishMsg(m *nats.Msg, opts ...nats.PubOpt) (*nats.PubAck, error)
34	}
35	
36	// Publisher publishes repo-operation jobs onto repo_ops_v1. Used by
37	// entire-core-global's webhook consumer to fan teardowns, App-suspends, and
38	// resumes out to the region that owns each placement.
39	type Publisher struct {
40		js JetStreamPublisher
41	}
42	
43	// NewPublisher binds a Publisher to a JetStream context.
44	func NewPublisher(js JetStreamPublisher) *Publisher {
45		return &Publisher{js: js}
46	}
47	
48	// PublishTeardown emits one teardown job for a single placement.
49	// Idempotent on the op + target ULID + observedAt via the Nats-Msg-Id
50	// dedup header. OTel trace context rides the NATS headers so the regional
51	// consumer's span parents to this publish.
52	//
53	// observedAt is the removal webhook's observation time; the consumer uses
54	// it as the last-writer-wins threshold for its skip-if-re-added gate.
55	func (p *Publisher) PublishTeardown(ctx context.Context, placement Placement, target Target, githubRepoID int64, observedAt time.Time) error {
56		return p.publishOp(ctx, OpTeardown, SuspendGateRemoval, placement, target, githubRepoID, 0, observedAt)
57	}
58	
59	// PublishAppSuspend emits one App-suspend job (installation.suspend) for a
60	// single placement. It stamps the installation-suspended gate and carries
61	// installationID, so the consumer gates it on the owning installation still
62	// being suspended rather than on repo re-observation. observedAt only feeds
63	// the dedup key here; the gate is current installation state, not
64	// observed-after. (The removal-driven PublishSuspend is gone — every
65	// GitHub-side removal tears down instead, COR-454.)
66	func (p *Publisher) PublishAppSuspend(ctx context.Context, placement Placement, target Target, githubRepoID, installationID int64, observedAt time.Time) error {
67		return p.publishOp(ctx, OpSuspend, SuspendGateInstallationSuspended, placement, target, githubRepoID, installationID, observedAt)
68	}
69	
70	// PublishResume emits one resume job for a single placement (App
71	// unsuspend). observedAt is the webhook's observation time; the resume
72	// consumer gates on CURRENT attachment rather than observed-after, so here
73	// it only feeds the dedup key.
74	func (p *Publisher) PublishResume(ctx context.Context, placement Placement, target Target, githubRepoID int64, observedAt time.Time) error {
75		return p.publishOp(ctx, OpResume, SuspendGateRemoval, placement, target, githubRepoID, 0, observedAt)
76	}
77	
78	func (p *Publisher) publishOp(ctx context.Context, op Op, gate SuspendGate, placement Placement, target Target, githubRepoID, installationID int64, observedAt time.Time) error {
79		parsed := ParsedSubject{Placement: placement, Op: op}
80		subject := Subject(parsed)
81		job := Job{Target: target, GitHubRepoID: githubRepoID, ObservedAt: observedAt, SuspendGate: gate, InstallationID: installationID}
82	
83		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(tracerName).Start(ctx, "repo.ops.publish",
84			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindProducer),
85			trace.WithAttributes(
86				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
87				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "publish"),
88				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", subject),
89				attribute.String("entire.operation", string(parsed.Op)),
90				attribute.String("entire.target_jurisdiction", placement.Jurisdiction),
91				attribute.String("entire.target_cluster_slug", placement.ClusterSlug),
92				attribute.String("entire.target_ulid", target.ULID),
93			),
94		)
95		defer span.End()
96	
97		data, err := Marshal(job)
98		if err != nil {
99			span.RecordError(err)
100			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "marshal repo-ops job")
101			return fmt.Errorf("marshal repo-ops job: %w", err)
102		}
103	
104		// Dedup key is op + target ULID + observation time. A producer retry of
105		// the same webhook collapses, but a later removal of the same placement
106		// after a re-add must enqueue separately; otherwise the stale first job
107		// can skip via the freshness gate and lose the real teardown/suspend.
108		// The op token keeps distinct ops for the same observation from
109		// collapsing into one job.
110		msgID := fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/%s", parsed.Op, target.ULID, observedAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
111		msg := &nats.Msg{Subject: subject, Data: data, Header: nats.Header{}}
112		msg.Header.Set(NatsMsgIDHeader, msgID)
113		otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Inject(ctx, headerCarrier(msg.Header))
114		span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("messaging.message.id", msgID))
115	
116		ack, err := p.js.PublishMsg(msg, nats.Context(ctx))
117		if err != nil {
118			span.RecordError(err)
119			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "nats publish")
120			return fmt.Errorf("publish repo-ops %s: %w", op, err)
121		}
122		span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("messaging.nats.duplicate", ack.Duplicate))
123		slogutil.Info(ctx, "published repo-ops job",
124			slog.String("op", string(op)),
125			slog.String("subject", subject),
126			slog.String("msg_id", msgID),
127			slog.String("target_ulid", target.ULID),
128			slog.Bool("duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
129		)
130		return nil
131	}
132	
133	// headerCarrier adapts nats.Header to the OTel TextMapCarrier contract.
134	type headerCarrier nats.Header
135	
136	func (c headerCarrier) Get(key string) string {
137		v := nats.Header(c).Values(key)
138		if len(v) == 0 {
139			return ""
140		}
141		return v[0]
142	}
143	func (c headerCarrier) Set(key, value string) { nats.Header(c).Set(key, value) }
144	func (c headerCarrier) Keys() []string {
145		keys := make([]string, 0, len(c))
146		for k := range c {
147			keys = append(keys, k)
148		}
149		return keys
150	}
151	
152	var _ propagation.TextMapCarrier = headerCarrier(nil)

37	// go to that cluster's NATS (configured via ENTIRE_MIRROR_GIT_NATS_URL).
38	type Publisher struct {
39		js JetStreamPublisher
40	}
41	
42	// NewPublisher binds a Publisher to a JetStream context.
43	func NewPublisher(js JetStreamPublisher) *Publisher {
44		return &Publisher{js: js}
45	}
46	
47	// PublishSyncRepo emits a single sync_repo job. Idempotent on
48	// (placement, source, target) via the Nats-Msg-Id dedup header — a
49	// retry within StreamDuplicatesWindow collapses server-side, so the
50	// caller doesn't have to coordinate. OTel trace context rides the
51	// NATS headers so the worker's span parents to this publish.
52	//
53	// A nil Publisher receiver or nil js panics on call: callers MUST
54	// wire a publisher, and serve-mode boot enforces it (see
55	// buildGitJobsPublisher). Silently treating nil as "skip the publish"
56	// is what stranded EU mirrors in provisioning state.
57	func (p *Publisher) PublishSyncRepo(ctx context.Context, placement Placement, source Source, target Target) error {
58		parsed := ParsedSubject{
59			Placement:  placement,
60			SourceKind: SourceKindGithub,
61			Op:         OpSyncRepo,
62		}
63		job := Job{Source: source, Target: target}
64		subject := Subject(parsed)
65	
66		spanAttrs := []attribute.KeyValue{
67			attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
68			attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "publish"),
69			attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", subject),
70			attribute.String("entire.operation", string(parsed.Op)),
71			attribute.String("entire.source_kind", string(parsed.SourceKind)),
72			attribute.String("entire.target_jurisdiction", placement.Jurisdiction),
73			attribute.String("entire.target_cluster_id", placement.ClusterID),
74			attribute.String("entire.source_owner", source.Owner),
75			attribute.String("entire.source_repo", source.Repo),
76			attribute.String("entire.target_ulid", target.ULID),
77		}
78	
79		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(tracerName).Start(ctx, "mirror.git.publish",
80			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindProducer),
81			trace.WithAttributes(spanAttrs...),
82		)
83		defer span.End()
84	
85		data, err := Marshal(job)
86		if err != nil {
87			span.RecordError(err)
88			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "marshal git job")
89			return fmt.Errorf("marshal git job: %w", err)
90		}
91	
92		// Msg-ID dedup key: same shape mirror-pipeline's resync-scheduler
93		// uses (op/source-kind/owner/repo/ulid). A retry of the *same*
94		// create-mirror call collapses; a separate placement on the same
95		// upstream gets a distinct key because target.ULID differs.
96		msgID := fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/%s/%s/%s",
97			parsed.Op, parsed.SourceKind,
98			source.Owner, source.Repo, target.ULID,
99		)
100		msg := &nats.Msg{
101			Subject: subject,
102			Data:    data,
103			Header:  nats.Header{},
104		}
105		msg.Header.Set(NatsMsgIDHeader, msgID)
106		otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Inject(ctx, HeaderCarrier(msg.Header))
107		span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("messaging.message.id", msgID))
108	
109		ack, err := p.js.PublishMsg(msg, nats.Context(ctx))
110		if err != nil {
111			span.RecordError(err)
112			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "nats publish")
113			return fmt.Errorf("publish git mirror job: %w", err)
114		}
115	
116		span.SetAttributes(
117			attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", int64(ack.Sequence)), //nolint:gosec // ack.Sequence is uint64; values that overflow int64 are out of scope
118			attribute.Bool("messaging.nats.duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
119		)
120		slogutil.Info(ctx, "published git mirror sync_repo",
121			slog.String("subject", subject),
122			slog.String("msg_id", msgID),
123			slog.String("source_owner", source.Owner),
124			slog.String("source_repo", source.Repo),
125			slog.String("target_ulid", target.ULID),
126			slog.Bool("duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
127		)
128		return nil
129	}
130	
131	// HeaderCarrier adapts nats.Header to the OTel TextMapCarrier contract so
132	// trace context propagates over JetStream. Exported so other entire-core NATS
133	// producers (e.g. the mirror-resync publisher) reuse the one adapter instead of
134	// re-copying it.
135	type HeaderCarrier nats.Header
136	
137	func (c HeaderCarrier) Get(key string) string {
138		v := nats.Header(c).Values(key)
139		if len(v) == 0 {
140			return ""
141		}
142		return v[0]
143	}
144	func (c HeaderCarrier) Set(key, value string) { nats.Header(c).Set(key, value) }
145	func (c HeaderCarrier) Keys() []string {
146		keys := make([]string, 0, len(c))
147		for k := range c {
148			keys = append(keys, k)
149		}
150		return keys
151	}
152	
153	var _ propagation.TextMapCarrier = HeaderCarrier(nil)
