25	// resyncWebhookPublisher publishes a synthetic GitHub "push" ForwardedWebhook
26	// onto the central webhooks_github_v1 JetStream (ENTIRE_NATS_URL, central US),
27	// which mirror-pipeline's existing fanout consumes to resync a repo (ENT-1172).
28	// It reuses the permswebhook envelope + subject constants (structurally
29	// identical to mirror-pipeline/pkg/webhookevents.ForwardedWebhook) and the
30	// gitjobs dedup-header constant, so this producer and the consumer can't drift.
31	//
32	// It publishes to the CENTRAL stream (cfg.NatsURL), NOT the in-cell mirror
33	// stream the gitJobsPublisher targets (cfg.MirrorGitNatsURL): the resync must
34	// land where cmd/fanout consumes, which is the central webhooks_github_v1.
35	type resyncWebhookPublisher struct {
36		js gitjobs.JetStreamPublisher
37	}
38	
39	var _ api.ResyncPublisher = (*resyncWebhookPublisher)(nil)
40	
41	func newResyncWebhookPublisher(js gitjobs.JetStreamPublisher) *resyncWebhookPublisher {
42		return &resyncWebhookPublisher{js: js}
43	}
44	
45	// resyncPushBody is the minimal GitHub push payload mirror-pipeline's fanout
46	// reads: only repository.full_name and installation.id (see
47	// ../mirror-pipeline/cmd/fanout/payloads.go). No ref/commits/after — the worker
48	// syncs AllRefs regardless. The installation id is required so a private
49	// checkpoints repo can mint an installation token.
50	type resyncPushBody struct {
51		Repository struct {
52			FullName string `json:"full_name"`
53		} `json:"repository"`
54		Installation struct {
55			ID int64 `json:"id"`
56		} `json:"installation"`
57	}
58	
59	// PublishResync builds and publishes the synthetic push webhook for repoID.
60	//
61	// DeliveryID buckets on the minute so the stream's ~5-min dedup window collapses
62	// a burst of resyncs from one busy repo into a single message (the free dedup
63	// win, not the deferred de-dup subsystem). OTel trace context rides the NATS
64	// headers so the fanout worker's span parents to this publish.
65	func (p *resyncWebhookPublisher) PublishResync(ctx context.Context, repoID model.RepoID, fullName string, installationID int64) error {
66		var body resyncPushBody
67		body.Repository.FullName = fullName
68		body.Installation.ID = installationID
69		rawBody, err := json.Marshal(body)
70		if err != nil {
71			return fmt.Errorf("marshal resync push body: %w", err)
72		}
73	
74		deliveryID := fmt.Sprintf("resync-%s-%d", repoID, time.Now().Unix()/60)
75		env := permswebhook.ForwardedWebhook{
76			DeliveryID: deliveryID,
77			Event:      "push",
78			Body:       rawBody,
79			ReceivedAt: time.Now(),
80		}
81		data, err := json.Marshal(env)
82		if err != nil {
83			return fmt.Errorf("marshal forwarded webhook: %w", err)
84		}
85	
86		subject := permswebhook.SubjectPrefix + "push"
87		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(resyncTracerName).Start(ctx, "mirror.resync.publish",
88			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindProducer),
89			trace.WithAttributes(
90				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
91				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "publish"),
92				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", subject),
93				attribute.String("entire.repo_id", repoID.String()),
94				attribute.String("entire.source_full_name", fullName),
95			),
96		)
97		defer span.End()
98	
99		msg := &nats.Msg{Subject: subject, Data: data, Header: nats.Header{}}
100		msg.Header.Set(gitjobs.NatsMsgIDHeader, deliveryID)
101		otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Inject(ctx, gitjobs.HeaderCarrier(msg.Header))
102		span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("messaging.message.id", deliveryID))
103	
104		ack, err := p.js.PublishMsg(msg, nats.Context(ctx))
105		if err != nil {
106			span.RecordError(err)
107			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "nats publish")
108			return fmt.Errorf("publish resync webhook: %w", err)
109		}
110	
111		span.SetAttributes(
112			attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", int64(ack.Sequence)), //nolint:gosec // ack.Sequence is uint64; values that overflow int64 are out of scope
113			attribute.Bool("messaging.nats.duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
114		)
115		slogutil.Info(ctx, "published mirror resync webhook",
116			slog.String("subject", subject),
117			slog.String("delivery_id", deliveryID),
118			slog.String("repo_id", repoID.String()),
119			slog.String("full_name", fullName),
120			slog.Int64("installation_id", installationID),
121			slog.Bool("duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
122		)
123		return nil
124	}
125	
126	// buildResyncPublisher returns a resync publisher bound to the CENTRAL NATS
127	// (cfg.NatsURL, where cmd/fanout consumes webhooks_github_v1) plus a cleanup
128	// that closes the connection. Unlike buildGitJobsPublisher — which requires
129	// NATS and fails boot — this degrades to a disabled (nil) publisher when
130	// cfg.NatsURL is unset, so a config without central NATS still boots; resync
131	// then returns ErrResyncUnavailable (503). In regional/standalone cfg.NatsURL
132	// is set in practice (the gitjobs publisher already requires a NATS URL).
133	func buildResyncPublisher(ctx context.Context, cfg Config) (*resyncWebhookPublisher, func(), error) {
134		if cfg.NatsURL == "" {
135			slogutil.Info(ctx, "mirror resync publisher disabled: ENTIRE_NATS_URL not set")
136			return nil, func() {}, nil
137		}
138		nc, err := connectNATSURL(ctx, cfg, cfg.NatsURL)
139		if err != nil {
140			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("resync nats connect: %w", err)
141		}
142		js, err := nc.JetStream()
143		if err != nil {
144			nc.Close()
145			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("resync jetstream context: %w", err)
146		}
147		cleanup := func() { drainNATS(ctx, nc, "resync") }
148		return newResyncWebhookPublisher(js), cleanup, nil
149	}

6		"log/slog"
7		"time"
8	
9		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg"
10		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
11		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"

17	)
18	
19	const tracerName = "entire.io/internal/entirecore/permssweep"
20	
21	// natsMsgIDHeader is the JetStream dedup header (same constant gitjobs and
22	// permsbackfill use; spelt out to avoid pulling in nats.go's internal const).
23	const natsMsgIDHeader = "Nats-Msg-Id"
24	
25	// publishTimeout bounds one synchronous PublishMsg round-trip. Load-bearing:
26	// the enumerator's ctx has no deadline, and PublishMsg with a deadline-free
27	// nats.Context waits for the PubAck indefinitely — with RetryOnFailedConnect
28	// the connect itself "succeeds" while NATS is down, so an unbounded publish
29	// would hang the CronJob forever instead of failing the tick loudly (the
30	// exact never-terminating-Job failure mode this fan-out exists to kill).
31	const publishTimeout = 15 * time.Second
32	
33	// JetStreamPublisher is the slice of nats.JetStreamContext the Publisher
34	// needs, pulled out so tests can stub publish without a live JetStream.
35	type JetStreamPublisher interface {
36		PublishMsg(m *nats.Msg, opts ...nats.PubOpt) (*nats.PubAck, error)
37	}
38	
39	// Publisher emits perms_sweep jobs onto the in-cell repo_ops_v1 stream. One
40	// Publisher per enumerator run; the subject is fixed at construction (the
41	// sweep is fleet-scoped, so every job of a run rides the same subject).
42	type Publisher struct {
43		js      JetStreamPublisher
44		subject string
45	}
46	
47	// NewPublisher binds a Publisher to a JetStream context and the enumerator's
48	// jurisdiction (empty publishes under the "global" token).
49	func NewPublisher(js JetStreamPublisher, jurisdiction string) *Publisher {
50		return &Publisher{js: js, subject: subjectFor(jurisdiction)}
51	}
52	
53	// publishMsg is the mechanical tail every perms_sweep publish shares —
54	// enumerator jobs, canaries, and the consumer's chunk continuations: build
55	// the message, stamp the JetStream dedup id, inject trace context, and run a
56	// publishTimeout-bounded PublishMsg (see publishTimeout for why the bound is
57	// load-bearing). Callers own their spans, metrics, and logging.
58	func publishMsg(ctx context.Context, js JetStreamPublisher, subject, msgID string, data []byte) (*nats.PubAck, error) {
59		msg := &nats.Msg{Subject: subject, Data: data, Header: nats.Header{}}
60		msg.Header.Set(natsMsgIDHeader, msgID)
61		otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Inject(ctx, natsmsg.HeaderCarrier(msg.Header))
62		pubCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, publishTimeout)
63		defer cancel()
64		return js.PublishMsg(msg, nats.Context(pubCtx)) //nolint:wrapcheck // every caller wraps with its own publish context
65	}
66	
67	// PublishSweep enqueues one per-installation sweep job carrying the
68	// enumerator's staleness cutoff. The Nats-Msg-Id (op/installation_id)
69	// collapses same-tick producer retries inside the stream's duplicates
70	// window; cross-tick duplicates are deliberately allowed and neutralized by
71	// the worker's consume-time work-list re-check.
72	func (p *Publisher) PublishSweep(ctx context.Context, installationID int64, staleBefore time.Time) error {
73		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(tracerName).Start(ctx, "perms.sweep.publish",
74			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindProducer),
75			trace.WithAttributes(
76				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
77				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "publish"),
78				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", p.subject),
79				attribute.Int64("entire.github.installation_id", installationID),
80			),
81		)
82		defer span.End()
83	
84		data, err := encodeEvent(installationID, staleBefore)
85		if err != nil {
86			span.RecordError(err)
87			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "encode sweep job")
88			return fmt.Errorf("encode sweep job: %w", err)
89		}
90	
91		msgID := fmt.Sprintf("%s/%d", op, installationID)
92		span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("messaging.message.id", msgID))
93	
94		ack, err := publishMsg(ctx, p.js, p.subject, msgID, data)
95		if err != nil {
96			span.RecordError(err)
97			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "nats publish")
98			recordInstallationPublished(ctx, "error")
99			return fmt.Errorf("publish perms sweep: %w", err)
100		}
101		recordInstallationPublished(ctx, "ok")
102		span.SetAttributes(
103			attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", natsmsg.ClampToInt64(ack.Sequence)),
104			attribute.Bool("messaging.nats.duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
105		)
106		slogutil.Debug(ctx, "published perms sweep job",
107			slog.String("subject", p.subject),
108			slog.String("msg_id", msgID),
109			slog.Int64("installation_id", installationID),
110			slog.Bool("duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
111		)
112		return nil
113	}
114	
115	// PublishCanary enqueues the enumerator's per-run liveness canary (see
116	// event.Canary). Deliberately NOT counted in installations_published — that
117	// counter is real sweep throughput. The constant Nats-Msg-Id only collapses
118	// same-tick producer retries: hourly ticks are far outside the stream's 10s
119	// duplicates window, so every run's canary is delivered.
120	func (p *Publisher) PublishCanary(ctx context.Context) error {
121		ctx, span := otel.Tracer(tracerName).Start(ctx, "perms.sweep.publish_canary",
122			trace.WithSpanKind(trace.SpanKindProducer),
123			trace.WithAttributes(
124				attribute.String("messaging.system", "nats"),
125				attribute.String("messaging.operation.type", "publish"),
126				attribute.String("messaging.destination.name", p.subject),
127				attribute.Bool("entire.permssweep.canary", true),
128			),
129		)
130		defer span.End()
131	
132		data, err := encodeCanaryEvent()
133		if err != nil {
134			span.RecordError(err)
135			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "encode sweep canary")
136			return fmt.Errorf("encode sweep canary: %w", err)
137		}
138	
139		msgID := op + "/canary"
140		span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("messaging.message.id", msgID))
141	
142		ack, err := publishMsg(ctx, p.js, p.subject, msgID, data)
143		if err != nil {
144			span.RecordError(err)
145			span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "nats publish")
146			return fmt.Errorf("publish perms sweep canary: %w", err)
147		}
148		span.SetAttributes(
149			attribute.Int64("messaging.nats.sequence", natsmsg.ClampToInt64(ack.Sequence)),
150			attribute.Bool("messaging.nats.duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
151		)
152		slogutil.Debug(ctx, "published perms sweep canary",
153			slog.String("subject", p.subject),
154			slog.Bool("duplicate", ack.Duplicate),
155		)
156		return nil
157	}

## Why

Phase 2 ([COR-984](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-984/go-nuts-phase-2-deepen-publishing-and-redelivery-apis), go-nuts v0.8.0) released the shared redelivery policy (`backoff.Policy`) and the legacy publishing adapter (`natsmsg.LegacyPublisher`), derived from exactly the code this repo hand-rolls. This PR retires those local copies so the delay math and publish prologue have one owner.

## What

- **go-nuts v0.7.0 → v0.8.0** (plus the matching otel/sdk 1.44 alignment).
- **repoops + permswebhook redelivery**: the duplicated geometric ×2 `nakDelay` / `deliveryCount` pair is replaced by a `backoff.Policy{Factor: 2}` per consumer (capped at `nakDelayMax` / `RetryBackoffMx` respectively). `DelayFor` computes the identical sequence, including the metadata-unavailable → base-delay edge; `NakOrTerm` with unlimited MaxDeliver always Naks, exactly as before. DLQ ordering (capture, then Ack; Nak on capture failure) and all Term paths are untouched. Tests now pin the exact delay envelope (5s, 10s, 20s, 30s cap) instead of just its shape.
- **Legacy publishers** (repoops, gitjobs, resync, permssweep incl. the consumer's chunk continuation, permsbackfill) publish through `natsmsg.LegacyPublisher`. Each keeps its domain: subjects, payloads, dedup keys, span names (via `Operation`), tracer names, metrics, and log lines are byte-identical. The local `headerCarrier` copies and `Nats-Msg-Id` constants are deleted. Email outbox, refevents, and resourceevents stay local on purpose — they have no duplicated prologue to converge (no producer span/inject; bespoke deadline classification).
- **Stale `natsx` references** in repoops/permswebhook comments removed (the mechanism lives in go-nuts/jsconsumer).

Deliberate behavior deltas, publish plumbing only:
- PubAck waits are now bounded (5s natsmsg default; permssweep keeps its load-bearing 15s) where four publishers previously waited on the caller ctx indefinitely. All callers already treat publish errors as retriable/best-effort.

No stream, durable, filter, subject, payload, message-ID, retry-delay, or disposition contract changes.

`medium effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify → ≤8 findings`

You are reviewing for **precision** at medium effort: every finding you surface
should be one a maintainer would act on.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, 3-state)

Dedup candidates that point at the same line/mechanism, keeping the one with
the most concrete failure scenario. For each remaining candidate, run **one
verifier** via the Agent tool: give it the diff, the relevant
file(s), and the candidate, and have it return exactly one of:

- **CONFIRMED** — can name the inputs/state that trigger it and the wrong
  output or crash. Quote the line.
- **PLAUSIBLE** — mechanism is real, trigger is uncertain (timing, env,
  config). State what would confirm it.
- **REFUTED** — factually wrong (code doesn't say that) or guarded elsewhere.
  Quote the line that proves it.

Keep candidates where the vote is CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 8 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 8 survive, keep the 8 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

1	// Package settingsconsumer durably consumes the repo_settings_v1 fan-out from
2	// this cell's LOCAL JetStream stream and converges each event onto the local
3	// repo_settings row(s).
4	//
5	// The fan-out is a BROADCAST bus (DESIGN Decision 6): every settings toggle in any
6	// cell is broadcast into every region's island, so this consumer binds the WHOLE
7	// stream (repo_settings.v1.>), NOT its own jurisdiction — the jurisdiction token on
8	// the wire is ORIGIN-tagging for observability, not routing. For each event it
9	// resolves the origin (repo_group_id → local repo_id via the reverse index; a
10	// native repo → its own placement) and LWW-upserts the full snapshot onto each
11	// local placement. A cell with no placement for the event acks and skips (the
12	// common case — most repos are not placed in most cells). The origin cell consumes
13	// its own broadcast too; the LWW guard makes that an idempotent no-op.
14	//
15	// It mirrors the per-cell decode consumers (internal/githubmeta, internal/githubpr):
16	// a durable pull consumer, AckExplicit, MaxDeliver-bounded, Term on a poison
17	// payload, Nak on a transient DB error, Ack on success or a benign no-placement
18	// skip. The caller gates Start behind CONSUME_REPO_SETTINGS so a cell without the
19	// stream provisioned doesn't error at CreateOrUpdateConsumer.
20	package settingsconsumer
21	
22	import (
23		"context"
24		"errors"
25		"log/slog"
26	
27		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
28		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
29		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes"
30		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
31	
32		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/otelsetup"
33		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/reposettings"
34		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/store"
35		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/jsconsumer"
36	)
37	
38	// consumerDurable is the durable consumer name on each cell's repo_settings_v1
39	// stream. One per deployment, stable across restarts.
40	const consumerDurable = "repo-settings-consumer"
41	
42	// consumerMaxDeliver caps redelivery before JetStream terms a message — same
43	// posture as the githubmeta / githubpr consumers.
44	const consumerMaxDeliver = 8
45	
46	// consumerCfg is the durable pull-consumer descriptor. It binds the WHOLE stream
47	// (repo_settings.v1.>): every cell must receive every settings event, then resolve
48	// local placement — filtering by own jurisdiction would drop the cross-cell
49	// broadcasts this consumer exists to apply (DESIGN Decision 6).
50	var consumerCfg = jsconsumer.Config{
51		Stream:        reposettings.StreamName,
52		Durable:       consumerDurable,
53		FilterSubject: reposettings.SubjectPrefix + ">",
54		MaxDeliver:    consumerMaxDeliver,
55		SpanName:      "repo_settings.consume",
56		Name:          "settingsconsumer",
57		// Tracer keeps consumer spans scoped to the service (otelsetup.tracerName),
58		// not the go-nuts module, so trace attribution is unchanged by the migration.
59		Tracer: otelsetup.Tracer(),
60	}
61	
62	// SettingsWriter is the store surface the consumer resolves placements and applies
63	// LWW upserts through, satisfied by *store.RepoStore.
64	type SettingsWriter interface {
65		LocalSettingsPlacements(ctx context.Context, repoID, repoGroupID string) ([]string, error)
66		ApplySettingsLWW(ctx context.Context, r store.SettingsRow) (applied bool, err error)
67	}
68	
69	// Consumer durably pulls repo_settings_v1 from this cell's LOCAL JetStream stream,
70	// bound to the WHOLE stream (broadcast=consume-all), and converges each event onto
71	// the local repo_settings row(s) under the LWW guard.
72	type Consumer struct {
73		nc    *nats.Conn
74		store SettingsWriter
75		m     metrics
76	
77		run *jsconsumer.Runner
78	}
79	
80	// NewConsumer constructs a Consumer over the local NATS connection and the store.
81	func NewConsumer(nc *nats.Conn, w SettingsWriter) *Consumer {
82		return &Consumer{nc: nc, store: w, m: newMetrics()}
83	}
84	
85	// Start creates the durable consumer and begins consuming. Returns immediately.
86	// The local repo_settings_v1 stream must already exist — it is provisioned
87	// declaratively in fleet (apps/nats-streams, nack), not by this binary. The caller
88	// gates Start behind CONSUME_REPO_SETTINGS so a cell without the stream provisioned
89	// doesn't error here.
90	func (c *Consumer) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
91		if c == nil || c.nc == nil {
92			return errors.New("settingsconsumer: Consumer not initialised")
93		}
94		if c.store == nil {
95			return errors.New("settingsconsumer: Consumer.store required")
96		}
97		run, err := jsconsumer.Start(ctx, c.nc, consumerCfg, func(msg jetstream.Msg) { c.handle(ctx, msg) })
98		if err != nil {
99			return err
100		}
101		c.run = run
102		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "repo_settings consumer started", slog.String("subject", consumerCfg.FilterSubject))
103		return nil
104	}
105	
106	// Stop halts the consume loop. Idempotent.
107	func (c *Consumer) Stop() error {
108		c.run.Stop()
109		return nil
110	}
111	
112	// handle is the per-message entry point (production callback + test seam): the shared
113	// span+decode-or-term prologue, then onEvent for a decoded event.
114	func (c *Consumer) handle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg) {
115		jsconsumer.Process(ctx, msg, consumerCfg, reposettings.Unmarshal, c.onEvent, func(ctx context.Context) {
116			c.m.dropped.Add(ctx, 1, attr("reason", "undecodable"))
117		})
118	}
119	
120	func (c *Consumer) onEvent(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, ev reposettings.Event) {
121		// DIRECTED event (new-placement inheritance, COR-901): the sender already
122		// resolved the exact target placement, so blind-write by repo_id — no local
123		// placement resolution. This is deliberately decoupled from the target's repos
124		// row existing: the seed rides a different stream (resource_lifecycle_v1) with
125		// independent backpressure, so requiring the row here would reintroduce the
126		// cross-stream race the directed push exists to avoid. There is no FK on
127		// repo_setting_kv.repo_id, so the row stands alone until the seed lands.
128		if ev.TargetRepoID != "" {
129			ok, err := c.store.ApplySettingsLWW(ctx, store.SettingsRow{
130				RepoID:      ev.TargetRepoID,
131				SettingKey:  ev.SettingKey,
132				Value:       ev.Value,
133				UpdatedFrom: ev.OriginCluster,
134				UpdatedAt:   ev.UpdatedAt,
135			})
136			if err != nil {
137				// Transient (DB blip) — nak for redelivery; the LWW upsert is idempotent.
138				span.RecordError(err)
139				span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "upsert")
140				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "settingsconsumer: apply directed settings failed; nak", slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("repo_id", ev.TargetRepoID))
141				_ = msg.Nak()
142				return
143			}
144			c.m.written.Add(ctx, 1, attr("mode", "directed"))
145			_ = msg.Ack()
146			outcome := "applied"
147			if !ok {
148				outcome = "noop" // lost the LWW guard (stale / a co-holder's identical push)
149			}
150			slog.InfoContext(ctx, "settingsconsumer: directed repo_settings event applied",
151				slog.String("outcome", outcome),
152				slog.String("repo_id", ev.TargetRepoID),
153				slog.String("repo_group_id", ev.RepoGroupID),
154				slog.String("origin_cluster", ev.OriginCluster),
155				slog.Time("updated_at", ev.UpdatedAt),
156				slog.String("setting_key", ev.SettingKey),
157				slog.Bool("value", ev.Value),
158			)
159			return
160		}
161	
162		// Resolve the event's origin to this cell's local placement(s). A DB blip here
163		// is transient — nak for redelivery.
164		placements, err := c.store.LocalSettingsPlacements(ctx, ev.RepoID, ev.RepoGroupID)
165		if err != nil {
166			span.RecordError(err)
167			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "resolve")
168			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "settingsconsumer: resolve local placement failed; nak", slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("origin_key", ev.OriginKey))
169			_ = msg.Nak()
170			return
171		}
172		if len(placements) == 0 {
173			// No placement in this cell — the common broadcast case (most repos aren't
174			// placed in most cells). A normal skip, not an error: ack so it doesn't
175			// redeliver. Debug-only (Decision 6: every toggle reaches every cell).
176			c.m.skipped.Add(ctx, 1)
177			slog.DebugContext(ctx, "settingsconsumer: no local placement; ack+skip",
178				slog.String("origin_key", ev.OriginKey), slog.String("repo_group_id", ev.RepoGroupID))
179			_ = msg.Ack()
180			return
181		}
182	
183		applied := 0
184		for _, repoID := range placements {
185			row := store.SettingsRow{
186				RepoID:      repoID,
187				SettingKey:  ev.SettingKey,
188				Value:       ev.Value,
189				UpdatedFrom: ev.OriginCluster,
190				UpdatedAt:   ev.UpdatedAt,
191			}
192			ok, err := c.store.ApplySettingsLWW(ctx, row)
193			if err != nil {
194				// Transient (DB blip) — nak the whole message for redelivery. The LWW
195				// upsert is idempotent, so re-applying the placements already written
196				// on the retry is a no-op (equal tuple).
197				span.RecordError(err)
198				span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "upsert")
199				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "settingsconsumer: apply settings failed; nak", slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("repo_id", repoID))
200				_ = msg.Nak()
201				return
202			}
203			if ok {
204				applied++
205			}
206			c.m.written.Add(ctx, 1)
207		}
208		_ = msg.Ack()
209	
210		// Settings toggles are low frequency, so one line per applied event is fine.
211		// outcome distinguishes a real convergence from an idempotent no-op (a stale
212		// event or the origin cell consuming its own broadcast, where the LWW guard
213		// changed nothing). setting_key/value carry the toggle state; no PII/payload here.
214		outcome := "applied"
215		if applied == 0 {
216			outcome = "noop" // every placement lost the LWW guard (stale / self-echo)
217		}
218		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "settingsconsumer: repo_settings event applied",
219			slog.String("outcome", outcome),
220			slog.String("repo_id", ev.RepoID),
221			slog.String("origin_key", ev.OriginKey),
222			slog.String("repo_group_id", ev.RepoGroupID),
223			slog.String("origin_cluster", ev.OriginCluster),
224			slog.Time("updated_at", ev.UpdatedAt),
225			slog.Int("placements", len(placements)),
226			slog.Int("applied", applied),
227			slog.String("setting_key", ev.SettingKey),
228			slog.Bool("value", ev.Value),
229		)
230	}

3	import (
4		"context"

6		"errors"
7		"fmt"

9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
12		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
13		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes"
14	
15		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/otelsetup"
16		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/store"
17		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg"
18	)
19	
20	// consumerDurable is the durable consumer name on each cell's github_pr_v1
21	// stream. One per deployment, stable across restarts.
22	const consumerDurable = "github-pr-consumer"
23	
24	// consumerMaxDeliver caps redelivery before JetStream terms a message — same
25	// posture as the github_meta / forwarder / ingest consumers.
26	const consumerMaxDeliver = 8
27	
28	// PullRequestWriter is the store sink the consumer upserts PR metadata into.
29	type PullRequestWriter interface {
30		UpsertGitHubPullRequestMeta(ctx context.Context, m store.GitHubPullRequestMeta) error
31	}
32	
33	// Consumer durably pulls github_pr_v1 from this cell's LOCAL JetStream stream,
34	// filtered to this placement's (jurisdiction, cluster) subject, and upserts each
35	// event into the local repo store keyed by (repo ULID, PR number).
36	//
37	// Display metadata only — it NEVER gates access. The producer (mirror-pipeline
38	// meta-fanout) publishes one Event per resolved placement into that placement's
39	// local NATS, so this consumer only ever sees events for repos in this cell.
40	type Consumer struct {
41		nc           *nats.Conn
42		store        PullRequestWriter
43		jurisdiction string
44		cluster      string
45		m            metrics
46	
47		cc jetstream.ConsumeContext
48	}
49	
50	// NewConsumer constructs a Consumer.
51	func NewConsumer(nc *nats.Conn, w PullRequestWriter, jurisdiction, cluster string) *Consumer {
52		return &Consumer{nc: nc, store: w, jurisdiction: jurisdiction, cluster: cluster, m: newMetrics()}
53	}
54	
55	// Start creates the durable consumer and begins consuming. Returns immediately.
56	// The local github_pr_v1 stream must already exist — it is provisioned
57	// declaratively in fleet (apps/nats-streams), not by this binary. The caller
58	// gates Start behind CONSUME_PULL_REQUESTS so a cell without the stream
59	// provisioned doesn't error here.
60	func (c *Consumer) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
61		if c == nil || c.nc == nil {
62			return errors.New("githubpr: Consumer not initialised")
63		}
64		if c.store == nil {
65			return errors.New("githubpr: Consumer.store required")
66		}
67		js, err := jetstream.New(c.nc)
68		if err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("githubpr: jetstream.New: %w", err)
70		}
71		subject := SubjectFor(c.jurisdiction, c.cluster)
72		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, StreamName, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
73			Durable:       consumerDurable,
74			AckPolicy:     jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
75			AckWait:       30 * time.Second,
76			MaxDeliver:    consumerMaxDeliver,
77			FilterSubject: subject,
78		})
79		if err != nil {
80			return fmt.Errorf("githubpr: create consumer %s/%s: %w", StreamName, consumerDurable, err)
81		}
82		cc, err := cons.Consume(func(msg jetstream.Msg) { c.handle(ctx, msg) })
83		if err != nil {
84			return fmt.Errorf("githubpr: consume %s: %w", subject, err)
85		}
86		c.cc = cc
87		go func() {
88			<-ctx.Done()
89			_ = c.Stop()
90		}()
91		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "github_pr consumer started",
92			slog.String("jurisdiction", c.jurisdiction), slog.String("cluster", c.cluster), slog.String("subject", subject))
93		return nil
94	}
95	
96	// Stop halts the consume loop. Idempotent.
97	func (c *Consumer) Stop() error {
98		if c.cc != nil {
99			c.cc.Stop()
100			c.cc = nil
101		}
102		return nil
103	}
104	
105	func (c *Consumer) handle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg) {
106		// Re-parent to the producer's publish span across the NATS hop.
107		ctx, span := natsmsg.StartConsumerSpan(ctx, otelsetup.Tracer(), msg, "github_pr.consume")
108		defer span.End()
109	
110		var ev Event
111		if err := json.Unmarshal(msg.Data(), &ev); err != nil {
112			// Poison payload — redelivery won't help. Term so it doesn't cycle.
113			span.RecordError(err)
114			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "decode")
115			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "githubpr: decode github_pr_v1; term", slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
116			c.m.dropped.Add(ctx, 1, attr("reason", "undecodable"))
117			_ = msg.Term()
118			return
119		}
120		if ev.RepoULID == "" || ev.Number == 0 {
121			// No key to upsert on — redelivery won't help. Term.
122			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "githubpr: github_pr_v1 missing repo_ulid or number; term",
123				slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()), slog.String("repo_ulid", ev.RepoULID), slog.Int("number", ev.Number))
124			c.m.dropped.Add(ctx, 1, attr("reason", "missing_key"))
125			_ = msg.Term()
126			return
127		}
128		ctx = otelsetup.WithBaggage(ctx, otelsetup.RepoIDAttr(ev.RepoULID))
129		if err := c.store.UpsertGitHubPullRequestMeta(ctx, toRow(ev)); err != nil {
130			// Transient (DB blip) — nak for redelivery.
131			span.RecordError(err)
132			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "upsert")
133			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "githubpr: upsert github_pull_request_meta failed; nak",
134				slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("repo_ulid", ev.RepoULID), slog.Int("number", ev.Number))
135			_ = msg.Nak()
136			return
137		}
138		c.m.written.Add(ctx, 1)
139		_ = msg.Ack()
140		// PR webhooks are low frequency, so a per-event success line is fine.
141		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "githubpr: github_pull_request_meta upserted",
142			slog.String("repo_ulid", ev.RepoULID), slog.Int("number", ev.Number))
143	}
144	
145	// toRow maps a decoded wire Event to the store row. Fields are copied verbatim;
146	// observed_at carries the producer's webhook-receipt time, the store's reorder
147	// guard. FullName is intentionally dropped — the serve path reads full_name from
148	// repos/github_repo_meta, keeping repo_id the single key.
149	func toRow(ev Event) store.GitHubPullRequestMeta {
150		return store.GitHubPullRequestMeta{
151			RepoID:     ev.RepoULID,
152			Number:     ev.Number,
153			GitHubPRID: ev.GitHubPRID,
154			Title:      ev.Title,
155			HTMLURL:    ev.HTMLURL,
156			State:      ev.State,
157			Draft:      ev.Draft,
158			HeadBranch: ev.HeadBranch,
159			UserLogin:  ev.UserLogin,
160			Body:       ev.Body,
161			CreatedAt:  ev.CreatedAt,

97	func (c *Consumer) handle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg) {

99		ctx, span := natsmsg.StartConsumerSpan(ctx, otelsetup.Tracer(), msg, "userlifecycle.consume")
100		defer span.End()
101	
102		var ev Event

108			c.m.dropped.Add(ctx, 1, attr("reason", "undecodable"))

111		}

114			// than churn redelivery on a misrouted event.
115			c.m.skipped.Add(ctx, 1, attr("reason", "not_user"))
116			_ = msg.Ack()
117			return
118		}
119		if ev.ResourceID == "" {
120			// No account to act on — redelivery won't help. Term.
121			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "userlifecycle: event missing account id; term", slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
122			c.m.dropped.Add(ctx, 1, attr("reason", "missing_account"))

124			return
125		}

128		case opDeleted:

130				span.RecordError(err)

135			}

138			// Account deletions are low frequency; this line doubles as a purge audit trail.
139			slog.InfoContext(ctx, "userlifecycle: user data purged", slog.String("account_id", ev.ResourceID))

141			// An op this consumer doesn't act on (additive producer contract) — ack.
142			c.m.skipped.Add(ctx, 1, attr("reason", "unhandled_op"))
143			_ = msg.Ack()
144		}

116	func (c *Consumer) handle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg) {
117		// Re-parent to the source-cluster publish span across the NATS hop.
118		ctx, span := natsmsg.StartConsumerSpan(ctx, otelsetup.Tracer(), msg, "user_activity.consume")
119		defer span.End()
120	
121		var ev UserActivityEvent
122		if err := json.Unmarshal(msg.Data(), &ev); err != nil {
123			// Poison payload — redelivery won't help. Term so it doesn't cycle.
124			span.RecordError(err)
125			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "decode")
126			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "forwarder: decode user_activity_v1; term", slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
127			_ = msg.Term()
128			return
129		}
130		if ev.Recipient == "" {
131			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "forwarder: user_activity_v1 missing recipient; term", slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
132			_ = msg.Term()
133			return
134		}
135		// Stamp the event identity into baggage so downstream spans (the DB upsert)
136		// and logs carry recipient/repo/type.
137		ctx = otelsetup.WithBaggage(ctx,
138			otelsetup.RecipientAttr(ev.Recipient), otelsetup.RepoIDAttr(ev.RepoID), otelsetup.ActivityTypeAttr(ev.Type))
139		if !c.recipientIsLocal(ev) {
140			// Should not happen given the placement subject filter; ack so a
141			// stray doesn't redeliver forever.
142			span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("entire.drop_reason", "foreign_placement"))
143			c.m.dropped.Add(ctx, 1, attr("reason", "foreign_placement"))
144			_ = msg.Ack()
145			return
146		}
147		// A facet enrichment event carries no row identity/counts — only facets for an
148		// already-forwarded checkpoint. Apply it as a facet-columns-only UPDATE keyed
149		// on (account, origin, checkpoint), never the row upsert (which would insert a
150		// phantom zero-count row and re-count the checkpoint).
151		if ev.Type == TypeCheckpointFacets {
152			if err := c.store.EnrichMyActivityFacets(ctx, ev.Recipient, store.OriginOf(ev.OriginKey, ev.RepoID), ev.RepoID, ev.CheckpointID,
153				ev.Skills, ev.McpServers, ev.ToolMix, ev.Labels); err != nil {
154				span.RecordError(err)
155				span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "enrich facets")
156				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "forwarder: enrich my_activity facets failed; nak", slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("recipient", ev.Recipient))
157				_ = msg.Nak()
158				return
159			}
160			c.m.written.Add(ctx, 1, attr("type", ev.Type))
161			_ = msg.Ack()
162			return
163		}
164		row := store.MyActivityRow{
165			AccountID: ev.Recipient,
166			Type:      ev.Type,
167			// A pre-v2 producer / unresolved repo sends no origin; the placement id
168			// is then the identity — byte-identical to the pre-origin key, so the
169			// mixed-version rollout window creates no new row shapes.
170			OriginKey:           ev.OriginKey,
171			RepoGroupID:         ev.RepoGroupID,
172			RepoID:              ev.RepoID,
173			Jurisdiction:        ev.Jurisdiction,
174			SHA:                 ev.SHA,
175			CheckpointID:        ev.CheckpointID,
176			CommittedAt:         time.Unix(ev.Timestamp, 0).UTC(),
177			Agent:               ev.Agent,
178			HasCheckpoint:       ev.HasCheckpoint,
179			InputTokens:         ev.InputTokens,
180			OutputTokens:        ev.OutputTokens,
181			CacheCreationTokens: ev.CacheCreationTokens,
182			CacheReadTokens:     ev.CacheReadTokens,
183			Steps:               ev.Steps,
184			SessionCount:        ev.SessionCount,
185			// Re-encode the wire []string ids to the raw-JSON form the spine stores, so
186			// the activity read scans them without decoding (only recap decodes them).
187			SessionIDs:    store.MarshalSessionIDs(ev.SessionIDs),
188			Additions:     ev.Additions,
189			Deletions:     ev.Deletions,
190			FilesChanged:  ev.FilesChanged,
191			SchemaVersion: ev.SchemaVersion,
192			State:         store.CommitState(ev.State),
193		}
194		if row.Agent == "" {
195			row.Agent = "unknown"
196		}
197		// Stream sequence is the monotonic guard for state. With one placement per
198		// repo, transitions for one (origin, sha) arrive in transition order and a
199		// higher seq is strictly newer. With several placements (mirrors), cells can
200		// interleave: a lagging cell's fresh publish of a stale state gets a newer
201		// seq and transiently wins — accepted, because that cell forwards the
202		// corrected state once its mirror syncs, so the row converges within sync
203		// lag. What the guard must (and does) still prevent is a REDELIVERY
204		// regressing a newer row: a redelivered message keeps its original seq. On
205		// the rare Metadata error, leave it 0 — the upsert then won't let this event
206		// regress an already-sequenced row.
207		if md, mdErr := msg.Metadata(); mdErr == nil {
208			row.StateSeq = int64(md.Sequence.Stream)
209		}
210		if err := c.store.UpsertMyActivity(ctx, row); err != nil {
211			// Transient (DB blip) — nak for redelivery.
212			span.RecordError(err)
213			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "upsert")
214			slog.WarnContext(ctx, "forwarder: upsert my_activity failed; nak", slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("recipient", ev.Recipient))
215			_ = msg.Nak()
216			return
217		}
218		c.m.written.Add(ctx, 1, attr("type", ev.Type))
219		_ = msg.Ack()
220	}

154	// JSPublisher is the minimal JetStream publish surface the forwarder needs.
155	// jetstream.JetStream satisfies it; tests inject a fake. JS publish (not core

162	// Publisher emits user_activity_v1 events into the recipient's HOME region.
163	//
164	// There is no supercluster: the publisher holds one JetStream context per
165	// jurisdiction (conns, keyed by jurisdiction) and publishes directly into the
166	// home region's stream, mirroring mirror-pipeline's cmd/fanout. A user_activity
167	// event is account-addressed and an account's residency unit is its
168	// jurisdiction, so the jurisdiction is the routing key — there is no per-account
169	// cluster to route by. Residency is enforced by WHICH region the event goes to,
170	// not by post-hoc filtering. Concurrency-safe (conns is read-only after
171	// construction) — share one across ingest workers.
172	type Publisher struct {
173		conns        map[string]JSPublisher // jurisdiction -> that region's JetStream
174		jurisdiction string                 // this deployment's jurisdiction
175		singleRegion bool                   // route unresolved-home events to the local region

179	// NewPublisher builds a Publisher over a jurisdiction->JetStream map.

181	// events with no resolved home to the local region instead of dropping them

183	func NewPublisher(conns map[string]JSPublisher, jurisdiction string, singleRegion bool) *Publisher {

187	// PublishUserActivity routes an event to its recipient's home region.
188	//
189	// Delivery contract (one contract, no "best-effort" ambiguity):
190	//   - returns nil  => handled: published, OR permanently skipped (no home /
191	//     unknown region / unroutable). The caller should ACK the source message;
192	//     redelivery would not change the outcome.
193	//   - returns err  => TRANSIENT failure (destination NATS unreachable). The
194	//     caller should NAK the source message so JetStream redelivers and we
195	//     retry the publish (idempotent downstream upsert makes this safe).
196	//
197	// Idempotent at the wire level — the downstream upsert is keyed by
198	// (account_id, repo_id, sha, type).
199	func (p *Publisher) PublishUserActivity(ctx context.Context, ev UserActivityEvent) error {
200		if p == nil {
201			return nil // forwarding disabled (nil publisher, e.g. tests)

Five consumers already run on go-nuts `jsconsumer` (settingsconsumer, mirrorlifecycle, repolifecycle, repogroupprimary, trailforgeevents); these four still hand-roll the identical `CreateOrUpdateConsumer`/`Consume`/ctx-watcher lifecycle and span+decode-or-term prologue that the scaffold owns. - **go-nuts v0.7.0 → v0.8.0** (the released Phase 2 version, same pin as entiredb).

Yes — in all three services, but the three bridge surfaces have very different usage profiles:

**`natsmsg.LegacyPublisher`** (the publish bridge) — 6 production call sites:
- entiredb: the five publishers this migration converted — repoops, gitjobs, resync, permssweep, permsbackfill
- mirror-pipeline: `internal/natspub`, behind all seven typed job publishers

**`natsmsg.LegacyJetStream` via the `DLQPublisher` alias** (the dead-letter publish surface) — this one is baked into the shared API itself: `natsmsg.DeadLetter` takes a `DLQPublisher`, which *is* `LegacyJetStream`. Users:
- entiredb: repoops, permssweep, permsbackfill, mirrordone consumers (DLQ capture)
- entire-api: analysis, ingest, jobsdlq (DLQ capture and the DLQ sweeper)

**`backoff`'s legacy bridges (`NakOrTermLegacy`, `NumDeliveredLegacy`, `IsFinalDeliveryLegacy`)** — **zero callers anywhere.** Phase 2 built them anticipating mirror-pipeline's legacy consumers would adopt the policy, but Phase 3 kept those fetch loops (fanoutengine, worker) fully local, and every consumer that did adopt `backoff` is on the modern `jetstream.Msg` API. They're dead weight today and could be deleted from go-nuts without touching any service.

So the realistic cleanup order is:

1. **backoff `*Legacy` set** — deletable now, no migration needed.
2. **`LegacyPublisher`** — goes away when the six publisher call sites swap their wiring from `nc.JetStream()` to `jetstream.New(nc)` and the modern `Publisher`. Mechanical but touches connection wiring in both repos.
3. **`LegacyJetStream`/`DLQPublisher`** — last, because `natsmsg.DeadLetter`'s own signature rides it; removing it means changing the shared DLQ API and all seven DLQ call sites across entiredb and entire-api.

One caveat on 2: the modern `Publisher.JS` field is the full `jetstream.JetStream` interface, so the swap also changes what tests fake — same friction that kept entire-api's forwarder publisher local. A narrow modern publish interface in natsmsg (mirroring `LegacyJetStream`) would make that migration clean; worth folding into the bridge-deletion ticket if you file it.
we should migrate off the legacy publisher no?

Yes — it was explicitly built as a transitional bridge ("a caller migrates by swapping the type, and the LegacyPublisher can be deleted once no caller remains"), and the longer it exists the more new code reaches for it. The migration is well-bounded:

**What it takes:**

1. **go-nuts first (small PR + release):** retype `Publisher.JS` from the concrete `jetstream.JetStream` interface to a narrow single-method publish interface (the modern mirror of `LegacyJetStream`). Non-breaking for real callers — `jetstream.JetStream` satisfies it — but it's what makes the service migrations clean, since today's single-method test fakes can't satisfy the full interface (the exact friction that kept entire-api's forwarder publisher local). Same PR can delete the `backoff` `*Legacy` set (zero callers anywhere).
2. **entiredb:** the five publishers swap `LegacyPublisher` → `Publisher`, and their wiring builds a modern `jetstream.New(nc)` handle alongside the legacy one (which the DLQ path still needs for `DeadLetter`).
3. **mirror-pipeline:** `natspub` swaps the same way; its seven typed publishers and their fakes shouldn't change at all if the narrow interface lands in go-nuts.
4. **go-nuts again:** delete `LegacyPublisher` once both services are off it.

**What it doesn't cover:** `LegacyJetStream` itself survives as `DeadLetter`'s publish surface (7 DLQ call sites across entiredb/entire-api), and mirror-pipeline's fanoutengine/worker fetch loops keep legacy contexts regardless. Modernizing `DeadLetter` could ride along — and if entire-api's ingest/analysis hold a legacy context *only* for DLQ capture, it would free that repo of the legacy API entirely — but it widens the change into the poison-path, which deserves its own review.

input.title: go-nuts Phase 4: retire the legacy JetStream publishing bridges
input.description:
## Context

Follow-up to COR-985. Phase 3 converged entiredb, entire-api, and mirror-pipeline onto go-nuts v0.8.0; the legacy `nats.JetStreamContext` publishing bridges were always documented as transitional. Current usage after Phase 3:

* `natsmsg.LegacyPublisher` — 6 call sites (entiredb repoops/gitjobs/resync/permssweep/permsbackfill publishers; mirror-pipeline `internal/natspub`).
* `natsmsg.LegacyJetStream` (as `DLQPublisher`, `DeadLetter`'s publish surface) — 7 DLQ call sites (entiredb repoops/permssweep/permsbackfill/mirrordone; entire-api analysis/ingest/jobsdlq).
* `backoff` `*Legacy` entry points — zero callers anywhere.

## Scope

### go-nuts (release v0.9.0)

* Add a narrow modern publish interface (the modern mirror of `LegacyJetStream`, satisfied by `jetstream.JetStream`) and retype `Publisher.JS` to it, so service tests keep single-method fakes.
* Retype `DLQPublisher`/`DeadLetter` onto the modern API (ctx-native `PublishMsg`).
* Delete `LegacyPublisher`, `LegacyJetStream`, and the `backoff` legacy bridges (`LegacyMsg`, `NakOrTermLegacy`, `NumDeliveredLegacy`, `IsFinalDeliveryLegacy`).
* Keep behavior identical on the modern path: span shape, `Nats-Msg-Id`, bounded PubAck, PubAck telemetry, DLQ provenance headers, publish-before-remove contract.

### Service migrations (one PR per service, pinning v0.9.0)

* entiredb: five publishers to `natsmsg.Publisher`; DLQ wiring to modern `jetstream.New(nc)` handles; test fakes to the modern signature.
* entire-api: DLQ surfaces (analysis, ingest, jobsdlq) to the modern API; drop the legacy `nats.JetStreamContext` handles where DLQ capture was their only use.
* mirror-pipeline: `internal/natspub` to `natsmsg.Publisher` (typed publishers keep their `Publication` seam); re-vendor. The worker/fanoutengine legacy fetch loops stay local (unchanged posture from Phase 3); webhookdlq stays local.

## Preservation gates

* Exact subjects, payloads, `Nats-Msg-Id` values, span names, messaging attributes, logs, and metrics.
* DLQ publication order (capture before Ack/Term; never remove on capture failure) and provenance headers.
* Publish timeout bounds as set in Phase 3 (5s default, permssweep 15s, natspub AckWait).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] go-nuts has no legacy `nats.JetStreamContext` publishing surface; `go test -race ./...` passes; v0.9.0 released.
- [ ] All three services pin v0.9.0; no service holds a legacy JetStream context for publishing or DLQ capture (fetch loops exempt).
- [ ] Embedded-NATS tests and `go test -race` pass per service; lint, `go mod tidy -diff`, vendoring, `git diff --check` clean.
- [ ] No stream, durable, subject, payload, message-ID, retry-delay, or disposition contract changes.

## Out of scope

Migrating mirror-pipeline's worker/fanoutengine fetch loops off the legacy consume API.

git add -A && git commit --quiet -m "natsmsg, backoff: retire the legacy JetStream publishing bridges (COR-1004)

Phase 3 (COR-985) moved every service onto the shared seams; the legacy
nats.JetStreamContext bridges were documented as transitional and can
now go:

- Publisher.JS is retyped from the concrete jetstream.JetStream to a
  narrow JetStream publish interface (the modern mirror of the deleted
  LegacyJetStream), so callers keep single-method test fakes instead of
  faking the full client. jetstream.JetStream satisfies it unchanged.
- DLQPublisher/DeadLetter move onto that modern surface (ctx-native
  PublishMsg); provenance headers, bounded publish, and the
  capture-before-dispose contract are unchanged.
- LegacyPublisher and LegacyJetStream are deleted; the shared publish
  core is inlined into Publisher.Publish now that one path remains.
- backoff's *Legacy entry points (LegacyMsg, NakOrTermLegacy,
  NumDeliveredLegacy, IsFinalDeliveryLegacy) had zero callers anywhere
  and are deleted, along with the disposer indirection that existed
  only to share logic between the two paths. natsmsgtest.FakeLegacyMsg
  goes with them.

The disposition matrix, publish span/header/ack contract, and DLQ
integration tests carry over on the modern path.
